item.title: Marathon champion Ruti Aga banned for six years after forging prescription from fake clinic
item.description: Investigators found the prescription for the banned substance was issued by a family member claiming to be a registered doctor.
item.content:encoded: Investigators found the prescription for the banned substance was issued by a family member claiming to be a registered doctor.

item.title: Sheehan switches to number eight for Munster derby
item.description: Dan Sheehan will captain Ireland in next month's Nations Championship games in Caelan Doris' absence [Getty Images] Leinster captain Dan Sheehan will start at number eight for the first time in Saturday's United Rugby Championship derby against Munster in Dublin. The Ireland hooker switches to the back row as one of four changes made by head coach Leo Cullen for the Aviva Stadium game (18:00 BST) following last weekend's 48-23 Investec Champions Cup victory over Clermont Auvergne. Ireland scrum-half Jamison Gibson-Park makes his first appearance of the season, while former Munster out-half Joey Carbery earns his first start since rejoining Leinster. Ronan Kelleher and Jamie Osborne are also drafted into the starting side, with Kelleher replacing Sheehan at hooker and Osborne joining Robbie Henshaw in midfield. The hosts are seeking consecutive URC victories after bouncing back from opening defeats by the Lions and Sharks with a convincing win over Cardiff. Leinster have collected eight points from their opening three league matches, including four bonus points. Munster, meanwhile, have made seven changes to the side that defeated Racing 92 in the Champions Cup last weekend. Shane Daly returns from injury, while Josh Wycherley, Kieran Brookes, Fineen Wycherley, Jack O'Donoghue, Alex Kendellen and Gavin Coombes are also drafted into the starting XV. Former Ireland Under-20 international Sean O'Brien switches from the wing to outside centre as he prepares to make his 50th Munster appearance. Mark Donnelly is in line for his first appearance of the season from the replacements' bench, with academy centre Gordon Wood also among the replacements. Tadhg Beirne and Craig Casey - the only Munster players in Andy Farrell's latest Ireland squad - both start. Munster have recovered from their opening URC defeat by Glasgow Warriors with a victory over the Bulls and a 26-26 draw against Ulster on October 10. Line-ups Leinster: Keenan; T O'Brien, Osborne, Henshaw, J O'Brien; Carbery, Gibson-Park; Porter, Kelleher, Furlong; J McCarthy, Ryan; Baird, Van der Flier, Sheehan (capt). Replacements: G McCarthy, Usanov, Clarkson, O'Tighearnaigh, Penny, Gunne, Gabriel, Tector. Munster: B O'Connor; McCarthy, S O'Brien, Nankivell, Daly; O'Shea, Casey; J Wycherley, Van der Merwe, Brookes; F Wycherley, Beirne (capt); O'Donoghue, Kendellen, Coombes. Replacements: Clein, Donnelly, Ala'alatoa, Edogbo, Gleeson, B O'Donovan, Hanrahan, Wood.

item.title: Ebola: South-East governments step up containment measures
item.description: — Place health workers, border teams on alert — Abia prepares isolation centres, seeks funds for protective gear — Enugu, Anambra intensify surveillance across LGAs By Anayo Okoli, Steve Oko, Vincent Ujumadu, Ugochukwu Alaribe, Jeff Agbodo and Emmanuel Iheaka Governments across the South-East have stepped up measures to prevent the spread of Ebola Virus Disease, following a reported case in Abuja, with Abia State preparing isolation facilities and seeking funds to procure protective equipment for health workers. Although no case of Ebola has been confirmed in any state in the zone, authorities said they were strengthening disease surveillance, alerting health workers and border teams, and improving emergency response capacity to contain any potential outbreak. The measures include heightened monitoring of suspected cases, public health awareness campaigns, infection prevention and control, and preparations to isolate and manage suspected cases. item.dc:creator: Nwafor
item.content:encoded: — Place health workers, border teams on alert — Abia prepares isolation centres, seeks funds for protective gear — Enugu, Anambra intensify surveillance across LGAs By Anayo Okoli, Steve Oko, Vincent Ujumadu, Ugochukwu Alaribe, Jeff Agbodo and Emmanuel Iheaka Governments across the South-East have stepped up measures to prevent the spread of Ebola Virus Disease, following a reported case in Abuja, with Abia State preparing isolation facilities and seeking funds to procure protective equipment for health workers. Although no case of Ebola has been confirmed in any state in the zone, authorities said they were strengthening disease surveillance, alerting health workers and border teams, and improving emergency response capacity to contain any potential outbreak. The measures include heightened monitoring of suspected cases, public health awareness campaigns, infection prevention and control, and preparations to isolate and manage suspected cases. Abia races to prepare isolation centres, seeks funds for protective gear Abia State Government said it had begun emergency preparedness measures against a possible Ebola outbreak, including plans to equip isolation facilities, procure personal protective equipment and intensify disease surveillance. The Permanent Secretary of the Abia State Ministry of Health, Dr Blossom Uma-Kalu, who disclosed this in an interview with Vanguard, assured residents that no case of Ebola had been recorded in the state. Uma-Kalu said the ministry had initiated consultations involving relevant departments and agencies to assess the state’s preparedness and identify gaps requiring urgent intervention. She, however, said additional funding was needed to procure personal protective equipment, PPE, thermometers, hand sanitisers and other essential supplies. According to her, the state was preparing a budget to determine which needs could be met through federal support and which would require state funding. “We have held meetings following communication from the Federal Ministry of Health about the case in Abuja. Health workers and relevant public health teams have been alerted to maintain a high index of suspicion,” she said. The Permanent Secretary said the government was also considering an additional isolation facility, while work continued on existing centres. She disclosed that the Infectious Disease Hospital (IDH) in Aba was nearing completion, while the isolation facility at a specialist hospital in Umuahia was undergoing remodelling. According to her, the state was also assessing a proposed facility that could be adapted for isolation if necessary. Uma-Kalu explained that establishing isolation centres required trained personnel, adequate funding and appropriate treatment and monitoring facilities, making it impractical to establish such centres in every local government area. She said the ministry was preparing a public health advisory to educate residents about Ebola, its symptoms and preventive measures. The advisory, she added, would include designated emergency telephone numbers for reporting suspected cases. Uma-Kalu urged health workers, particularly those in private hospitals and laboratories, to remain vigilant and pay attention to patients’ travel histories and symptoms that could suggest Ebola infection. She said public health teams working in communities and at entry points into the state had also been alerted to watch out for possible cases. The Permanent Secretary advised residents to remain calm but vigilant, avoid unnecessary contact with the blood and other body fluids of suspected cases, and observe appropriate infection-prevention measures. She cautioned against dismissing suspicious symptoms as ordinary malaria without proper medical assessment. “People should not be afraid, but they need to be vigilant. Health workers must maintain a high index of suspicion and ensure that cases with symptoms suggestive of Ebola are properly assessed,” she said. She urged residents to rely on verified public health information rather than panic, adding that the state was taking steps to prepare for any eventuality. Enugu intensifies surveillance across 17 LGAs Enugu State Government said it had intensified disease surveillance across its 17 local government areas and reactivated its Public Health Emergency Operations Centre following the reported Ebola case in the country. The Commissioner for Health, Prof. George O. Ugwu, who disclosed this in an interview with Vanguard, reassured residents that no case of Ebola Virus Disease had been confirmed in the state. “Let me begin by reassuring the people of Enugu State that there is currently no confirmed case of Ebola Virus Disease in Enugu State,” he said. Ugwu said the government was strengthening preparedness in collaboration with the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC), the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, Port Health Services, airport authorities and other relevant partners. He noted that Enugu’s position as a major travel and commercial hub, particularly through the Akanu Ibiam International Airport, made heightened surveillance necessary. According to him, surveillance had been reinforced across the state, while rapid response teams and technical personnel remained on standby to respond to suspected cases. The commissioner urged public and private health facilities to remain alert, promptly isolate suspected cases in line with established protocols and report them to the appropriate Disease Surveillance and Notification Officer (DSNO) or the state emergency operations centre. He also advised health workers to maintain strict infection prevention and control measures, including the use of appropriate protective equipment. Ugwu urged residents to remain calm, practise proper hand hygiene, avoid contact with the body fluids of sick persons and promptly report suspected cases to health authorities. He cautioned against rumours, misinformation and stigmatisation, advising the public to rely on verified information from the state Ministry of Health, the NCDC and other recognised health authorities. He assured residents that the government would continue working with relevant agencies to strengthen Ebola preparedness, surveillance and response. Anambra to deploy surveillance officers at airport, motor parks Anambra State Government announced plans to deploy surveillance officers at strategic locations, including the Chinua Achebe International Airport, Umueri, motor parks, banks and other public places to strengthen efforts to prevent the spread of Ebola. The Commissioner for Health, Dr Afam Ben Obidike, who disclosed this while briefing reporters in Awka, said the officers would screen passengers arriving in the state from Abuja, Lagos and other African countries. He urged residents not to panic, assuring them that the government was taking measures to prevent an outbreak. Obidike said the state had monitored 40 persons of interest, with 33 completing their monitoring period and being cleared, while seven remained under active follow-up. He said all seven were stable. According to him, Anambra had developed an Ebola preparedness and operational plan covering surveillance, rapid response, infection prevention and control, laboratory coordination, referral arrangements, risk communication and logistics. He added that the state’s surveillance network across the 21 local government areas, the airport, motor parks and other public places would be strengthened to ensure early detection and reporting. The commissioner said state surveillance officers had participated in a two-day online training organised by the NCDC on monitoring persons of interest. He urged disease surveillance officers, health facilities and community reporting networks to promptly report unusual illnesses or deaths. He also advised healthcare workers to observe infection-prevention protocols and obtain patients’ travel and exposure

item.title: Chris Pratt Officially Confirms Star-Lord's Return to the MCU
item.description: We haven't seen Chris Pratt's Star-Lord in the Marvel Cinematic Universe since 2023, when James Gunn's Guardians of the Galaxy trilogy definitively concluded . Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3 ended on a hard reset for Star-Lord (aka Peter Quill), with the intergalactic hero returning to Earth and finding new purpose: enjoying Terran cereal and contemplating an amateur career in landscaping.

item.title: Los Angeles Chargers news: Omarion Hampton still ranked highly among 2nd-year backs
item.description: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - OCTOBER 18: Linebacker Nick Bolton #32 of the Kansas City Chiefs tackles running back Omarion Hampton #8 of the Los Angeles Chargers in the second quarter at Arrowhead Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s been a rough season thus far for Omarion Hampton. He was supposed to be one of the best young backs in the league. NFL insider Jordan Schultz at one point made a bold prediction that Hampton would lead the NFL in scrimmage yards while finishing with 12+ touchdowns. He’s currently barely on pace for that amount of touchdowns and you can’t lead the league in yards from scrimmage if you are barely on the field. That’s what it’s been like for the 23-year old who came into the league with the expectation that he’d be a lead guy for a team. Hard to imagine he’s in any kind of good spirits since the two lost fumbles in the first two weeks of this season. But despite that, outside of the team, there are believers. Take Bleacher Report’s Gary Davenport who just recently re-ranked the second-year backs in the league. Hampton came in third, behind only Ashton Jeanty and TreyVeon Henderson. “ Omarion Hampton has had little opportunity to establish a rhythm. ” “ When the 23-year-old was drafted 22nd overall last year, it was with the expectation that he would be the Chargers’ lead back from the jump. He was widely considered a first-round talent after a wildly productive two-season stretch at North Carolina. ” “ An ankle injury sidelined Hampton for almost half his rookie season, but he was effective when available. He averaged 4.4 yards per carry, scored five touchdowns and contributed just under 82 total yards per game. Then 2026 rolled around, and the wheels came off. ” “The winless Chargers are a mess, and Mike McDaniel’s decision to use a three-back committee has done little to help Hampton find his groove. Hampton has exceeded 15 carries just once this season, while his yards-per-carry average has dropped by nearly a full yard. ” “ The talent is there, but the situation is a nightmare. ” Do you think Davenport is correct to still hold Hampton in such high regard? Should he be lower based on his current situation? Let us know below! And now for today’s links. item.title: Maryland staffer called cops on student journalists reporting on Mike Locksley firing
item.description: Tommy Gilligan-Imagn Images Maryland staffer called cops on student journalists reporting on Mike Locksley firing appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Maryland football decided to move on from Mike Locksley on Wednesday. Locksley was fired after dropping to 2-5 this season and 39-54 overall as head coach, which included an interim stint back in 2015. In the aftermath of the termination, student journalists for the Testudo Times, the student-run Maryland athletic news site, were questioned by police , per a post by Nolan Rogalski of the Testudo Times. “For @testudotimes, @JudeWilkenfeld and I were outside Jones-Hill House trying to get players to comment. An athletics staffer took pictures of us, and a police dispatch was called for suspicious activity; a cop and 2 cop cars pulled up, and officers ID’d us and asked us to leave,” the post from Rogalski on X, formerly Twitter, read. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The students appeared not to be causing harm nor doing anything that would be deemed illegal. It is unknown why the staffer called the police. Still, it is common practice for student-run news affiliates to try to get comments after a coach is let go. Last season, by this point in October, seven coaches had already been fired, and in most cases, student-run news outlets tried to get comments. A spokesperson on behalf of the University of Maryland Police Department and Maryland Athletics released a statement regarding the interaction . “UMPD was contacted today, October 21, 2026, about two individuals who were standing outside of Jones Hill House. Due to heightened concerns for staff and player safety around the football program in recent weeks, there has been increased security around athletics facilities. A UMPD officer approached the two individuals, learned they were with a campus media organization, recorded student IDs, and no report was taken. UMPD and Maryland Athletics respect the First Amendment rights of all journalists reporting in public spaces,” the statement read. Maryland is off this week as they move to their interim coach. Their next game is a home date against Illinois on October 31. Related: Oregon’s Dante Moore, Evan Stewart rules out for Illinois clash Related: Oregon’s Jamari Johnson cited for speeding on same night Evan Stewart was arrested

item.title: Jurgen Klopp picks Barcelona over Real Madrid ahead of crucial El Clasico: ‘I support the better team’
item.description: Jurgen Klopp picks Barcelona over Real Madrid ahead of crucial El Clasico: ‘I support the better team’ Jurgen Klopp believes Barcelona are currently the stronger side ahead of Sunday’s El Clasico, backing Hansi Flick’s team to have the edge over Real Madrid despite their contrasting results in the Champions League. The German head coach will be watching the showdown at Spotify Camp Nou , where Barcelona can strengthen their position at the top of La Liga and extend their six-point advantage over their fiercest rivals with a victory. The former Liverpool manager also revealed why he used to favour Barcelona when watching the rivalry, pointing to his dislike of Real Madrid’s defensive approach during the era of Pepe. Klopp now considers himself a neutral observer, but his assessment of the teams’ current levels gives Barcelona a strong endorsement ahead of a fixture that could have a significant impact on the title race. Klopp explains why he favours Barcelona over Real Madrid Klopp confirmed that El Clasico remains a fixture he has followed throughout his life, regardless of where he has been working. Jurgen Klopp has backed Barcelona for El Clasico. (Photo by Maja Hitij/Getty Images) His historical preference for Barcelona, however, was shaped by his reaction to the way Madrid defended during some of the rivalry’s most intense encounters. “Of course I’ll watch El Clasico between Barcelona and Real Madrid. I’ve watched this game at every stage of my life. “In the past, I was more of a Barcelona supporter because I used to hate it when Pepe and the other defenders used to clear everything out of the way back then. “That’s the only reason I always supported Barça. These days, I watch it with a neutral perspective. “Today, I support the better team. And looking at things at the moment, that is probably Barcelona,” he told Buli News . Barcelona face Real Madrid with six-point lead at stake Barcelona are the favourites to beat Real Madrid. (Photo by Franco Arland/Getty Images) Barcelona enter the Clasico six points ahead of Real Madrid, giving the contest added importance. A home victory would allow Flick’s side to increase that margin and put further pressure on their rivals early in the campaign. However, Barcelona’s preparations have not been entirely straightforward, as their first defeat of the season came against Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League, with the French side exposing defensive weaknesses and securing a 4-2 victory. Real Madrid, by contrast, head into the weekend after beating RB Leipzig 4-1 in Europe. That result offers the visitors a confidence boost and presents a different picture from the league standings, where Barcelona hold the advantage.

item.title: Elephant Rumblings: Kotsay Staying Put?
item.description: CLEVELAND, OHIO - SEPTEMBER 20: Umpire Stu Scheurwater #85 argues with manager Mark Kotsay #7 of the Athletics after Kotsay was ejected during the third inning against the Cleveland Guardians at Progressive Field on September 20, 2026, in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images Happy Thursday everyone! The World Series is nearly upon us. Just one more day before baseball fans are treated to Game 1 of the Fall Classic between the Milwaukee Brewers and the Tampa Bay Rays. Neither team has won the World Series so one way or another, one organization is going to taste the sweet feeling of hoisting the Commissioner’s Trophy within the next two weeks. And for A’s fans, there aren’t any major former Athletics on these teams (sorry Jorge Mateo and Chad Patrick ). Still, there is a sense of comradery among the fanbases. Tampa and Milwaukee have been low-spenders for the majority of their existences, much like the Athletics. Getting to watch one of these low-payroll franchises lift that final trophy will be awesome to watch for A’s fans. A remind that even against the highest-spending teams like the Dodgers and Yankees, any team can win on any day in baseball. Anyway, now that the A’s have their top voice in the front office, it’s time for Taylor Smith to begin staffing that office. And that’s something that the team is starting on immediately. And based off the comments from yesterday’s presser, it sounds like Smith will be hiring a GM to work under him. That’s not a shock considering that’s how most front offices work in baseball these days. Now we have to see who Smith will tab as his second-in-command. Furthermore, from that same presser it sounds like manager Mark Kotsay’s job is safe, at least for now: Taylor Smith and A’s manager Mark Kotsay will have dinner tonight in Vegas. Smith: “From my conversations with Mark so far, he seems like a great guy. Someone who's hungry for all the information we can get [the coaching staff], and I think it'll be a great partnership.” — Martín Gallegos (@MartinJGallegos) October 21, 2026 That doesn’t sound like someone who is getting ready to make a change in the dugout. item.title: Ebola: Tomori faults Nigeria’s response timeline, demands full disclosure
item.description: …Warns against complacency By Sola Ogundipe Renowned Virologist and chairman of the West African National Academy of Scientists, Professor Oyewale Tomori, has raised concerns over the time it took Nigerian health authorities to confirm the country’s Ebola case, warning that delays in diagnosis and incomplete public information could undermine confidence in the national response. Tomori’s concerns come amid questions about the circumstances surrounding the confirmed case, the patient’s travel history and the adequacy of Nigeria’s preparedness to contain the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola virus disease. He warned that Nigeria must combine transparent communication with effective surveillance, rapid diagnosis, comprehensive contact tracing and adequate treatment and isolation capacity to prevent the outbreak from escalating. Speaking during a television interview, the virologist said he was more confident about Nigeria’s preparedness after hearing the health minister outline measures being taken to contain the outbreak, but stressed that the country must not become complacent. Tomori said the interval between the time the patient’s reported onset of symptoms and confirmation of the infection was a cause for concern, stressing that Nigeria must strengthen its disease surveillance, improve early diagnosis and prepare for the possibility of additional cases. He called on the Federal Government to provide comprehensive information about the case, including the patient’s movements before diagnosis and the extent of contact tracing, warning that gaps in official communication would inevitably fuel rumours. “The government must be completely transparent about matters like this. We don’t want to hear information in bits and pieces from different sources. Initially, we were told that the woman came from Uganda, later I heard the Ugandan authorities say she was a transit passenger. We need complete information, and when the government fails to provide it, the gaps are filled with rumours. “Tell us where the samples were tested and provide the relevant details. We are now hearing that the woman is a diplomat’s wife, among other reports. Certain information may need to remain confidential, but this is a national emergency, it concerns all of us, and we need the facts. We also need a clearer explanation of how the woman entered the country and what happened after her arrival. “Where did she stay? Where did she go? item.content:encoded: …Warns against complacency By Sola Ogundipe Renowned Virologist and chairman of the West African National Academy of Scientists, Professor Oyewale Tomori, has raised concerns over the time it took Nigerian health authorities to confirm the country’s Ebola case, warning that delays in diagnosis and incomplete public information could undermine confidence in the national response. Tomori’s concerns come amid questions about the circumstances surrounding the confirmed case, the patient’s travel history and the adequacy of Nigeria’s preparedness to contain the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola virus disease. He warned that Nigeria must combine transparent communication with effective surveillance, rapid diagnosis, comprehensive contact tracing and adequate treatment and isolation capacity to prevent the outbreak from escalating. Speaking during a television interview, the virologist said he was more confident about Nigeria’s preparedness after hearing the health minister outline measures being taken to contain the outbreak, but stressed that the country must not become complacent. Tomori said the interval between the time the patient’s reported onset of symptoms and confirmation of the infection was a cause for concern, stressing that Nigeria must strengthen its disease surveillance, improve early diagnosis and prepare for the possibility of additional cases. He called on the Federal Government to provide comprehensive information about the case, including the patient’s movements before diagnosis and the extent of contact tracing, warning that gaps in official communication would inevitably fuel rumours. “The government must be completely transparent about matters like this. We don’t want to hear information in bits and pieces from different sources. Initially, we were told that the woman came from Uganda, later I heard the Ugandan authorities say she was a transit passenger. We need complete information, and when the government fails to provide it, the gaps are filled with rumours. “Tell us where the samples were tested and provide the relevant details. We are now hearing that the woman is a diplomat’s wife, among other reports. Certain information may need to remain confidential, but this is a national emergency, it concerns all of us, and we need the facts. We also need a clearer explanation of how the woman entered the country and what happened after her arrival. “Where did she stay? Where did she go? How many people did she come into contact with?” he asked, stressing that these details were essential to establishing the extent of possible exposure and reassuring the public,” he queried. Tomori warned that the time taken to confirm the infection highlighted the need for healthcare workers to maintain a high index of suspicion when treating patients who have travelled from areas experiencing Ebola outbreaks. On the timeline, Tomori said the period was still within the incubation period. “However, the fact that it took until the 20th (October) to confirm the case is a concern and we need to improve on that. By the time the woman had moved between different locations, the opportunity for further exposure might already have arisen. “We faced a similar problem in 2014, when Patrick Sawyer arrived in Nigeria. It took about three or four days to diagnose him. Samples were initially being sent for malaria testing. When someone arrives from an area experiencing an outbreak, our level of awareness should be much higher. “The first disease that should come to mind is the one circulating in the area from which the person has travelled, not malaria, which is common in our environment. Our healthcare workers need to understand this. Their own lives are also at risk, so they must remain alert. “If I hear that someone has arrived from a country experiencing an Ebola outbreak, or from an area close to one, my first question would be whether the person could have Ebola before considering other possibilities. “We need to move beyond routine thinking before concluding that someone has malaria, healthcare workers should be up to date on diseases circulating in the places from which their patients have travelled,” he noted. On contact tracing Tomori said the health authorities need to gather more information and identify as many contacts as possible. “We should have more details than we currently have. For now, there is no reason to panic, the authorities are putting the necessary measures in place. What we need to do is prepare for the worst-case scenario. Suppose two or three of those contacts test positive. What happens next? “Do we have the hospitals, isolation facilities and other resources needed to manage additional cases? Those are the questions we should be asking now, rather than assuming that everyone will die because Ebola has entered the country. There are 44 people reportedly under quarantine. If one, two or three become infected, we must be ready to respond. According to him, healthcare workers must look beyond common illnesses such as malaria when a patient’s travel history suggests possible exposure to a dangerous infectious disease. “When someone arrives from an area experiencing an outbreak, our level of awareness should be much higher. The first disease that should come to mind is the one circulating in the area from which the person has travelled, not malaria, which is common in our environment.” He warned that failure to recognise the possibility of Ebola early could expose healthcare workers and other patients to infection. “I think the authorities need to gather more information and identify as many contacts as possible. We should have more details than we currently have,” he said. He said Nigeria should plan for the worst-case scenario without creating unnecessary public alarm. “For now, there is no reason to panic. The authorities are putting the necessary measures in place,” he said, adding that preparedness would be critical if the outbreak expanded. Further, Tomori also cautioned against relying exclusively on geographical distance to assess Nigeria’s risk. He said although the World Health Organisation had reportedly classified the country as being at low risk, he argued that regular travel between Nigeria and affected regions needed to be considered. “Hundreds of Nigerians travel to the region for business and other activities before returning home. That makes the risk more complicated than simply measuring the distance between two locations,” he said. On the strain responsible for the outbreak, Tomori explained that Ebola viruses differ in their characteristics and severity, even though they belong to the same broader group. “The Zaire strain has recorded fatality rates approaching 90 per cent in some outbreaks, while the Sudan strain has recorded rates of around 60 per cent. Bundibugyo has recorded fatality rates of about 50 per cent in some outbreaks,” he said. He cautioned against interpreting the comparatively lower fatality rate as evidence that the strain was harmless. “When we say Bundibugyo is less severe, however, that does not mean it is harmless or that it cannot kill people,” he said. The post Ebola: Tomori faults Nigeria’s response timeline, demands full disclosure appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 🚨 Blow for Bayern, star ruled out indefinitely!
item.description: 🚨 Blow for Bayern, star ruled out indefinitely! A major blow for Bayern Munich! Despite only coming on in the 68th minute against Arsenal yesterday, Luis Diaz had to leave the field in the 90th minute after suffering a thigh injury. This Thursday, Bayern Munich confirmed the bad news in a statement. The Colombian forward suffered a "minor hamstring tear". However, questions remain over Luis Diaz's return date, as Bayern Munich said their forward would be sidelined "indefinitely". The Bavarian club will therefore have to rely on youngster Lennart Karl, Serge Gnabry or Alphonso Davies. This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. item.title: Charles Davalan singles, plus Brent Honeywell Jr. in Dominican Winter League
item.description: Oct 18, 2024; New York City, New York, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers relief pitcher Brent Honeywell (40) reacts during the fourth inning of game five of the NLCS against the New York Mets during the 2024 MLB playoffs at Citi Field. Mandatory Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con Wednesday was light in Dodgers action in the Arizona Fall League, as the Glendale Desert Dogs were shut out in a game shortened by rain to only six innings. Against the Peoria Javelinas, Glendale managed only four hits, all singles, one of them by second baseman Charles Davalan. So let’s expand our offseason minor league scope a bit, and turn to the Dominican Winter League (or LIDOM, if you prefer). As far as I can tell, shortstop Emil Morales is the only Dodgers minor leaguer currently active in the league, which started its season last Friday. Morales, who by season’s end was ranked the No. 22 prospect in baseball by MLB Pipeline and ranked 29th by Baseball America , did not play on Wednesday, but has played in two of five games thus for for Gigantes del Cibao. Morales, who turned 20 in September, has a single, double, and two walks in his seven plate appearances thus far. He’s the second-youngest player on the Gigantes, with Rockies prospect Ronny Brito, a switch-hitting infielder/outfielder five and a half months younger than Morales. Someone who did play on Wednesday was old friend Brent Honeywell Jr., the former Dodgers pitcher, official “dawg” during the 2024 postseason and unofficial NLCS MVP that year . Honeywell suffered some injury that cost him most of the last two seasons, and pitched in seven games for Triple-A El Paso, a San Diego Padres affiliate. The first of those games for El Paso was at Oklahoma City on August 29 , his first game action since Game 4 of the 2024 World Series . Honeywell for the Gigantes on Wednesday pitched a scoreless sixth inning in relief. This is the second time in his career the 31-year-old right-hander has played in a winter league, having also pitched in seven games and 28 innings for Escogido in the 2022-23 season. Wednesday scores Peoria 3, Glendale 0 (6 innings) Gigantes del Cibao 14, Leones del Escogido 9 Thursday schedule 4 p.m. PT: Gigantes del Cibao vs. Toros del Este (on MLBtv) 6:30 p.m.: Glendale at Mesa Solar Sox ( AFL live streams )

item.title: Reps pass bill for National Children’s Hospital in Imo
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina,Abuja The House of Representatives has passed for second reading a bill seeking to establish a National Children’s Hospital in Ideato, Imo State, to expand access to specialised paediatric healthcare and reduce child mortality in Nigeria. The bill, sponsored by the member representing Ideato North and South Federal Constituency, Ikenga Imo Ugochinyere, scaled the second-reading hurdle after lawmakers considered its general principles during plenary. Leading the debate, Ugochinyere said the proposed hospital would provide specialised medical services for children, strengthen the country’s capacity to manage complex childhood illnesses and improve access to quality healthcare. The lawmaker said the proposed legislation was in line with the constitutional responsibility of government to protect the welfare of citizens, particularly children, who remain among the most vulnerable members of society. He cited Section 14(2)(b) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, which provides that the security and welfare of the people shall be the primary purpose of government. According to him, the provision places an obligation on government to prioritise accessible, affordable and quality healthcare for Nigerians, including children. Ugochinyere also expressed concern over Nigeria’s child mortality burden, noting that preventable conditions such as malaria, pneumonia, diarrhoeal diseases and neonatal complications continue to threaten the survival and healthy development of children. He argued that a dedicated national paediatric hospital would improve the diagnosis and treatment of complex childhood diseases while supporting medical research, professional training and early intervention services. The lawmaker further referenced Section 13 of the Child Rights Act, 2003, which recognises every child’s right to the best attainable state of physical, mental and spiritual health. He said the proposed hospital would provide an institutional framework for advancing child-centred medical care and improving health outcomes. Drawing comparisons with specialised paediatric institutions in other countries, Ugochinyere cited Children’s National Hospital in Washington, D.C., United States, and the Red Cross War Memorial Children’s Hospital in Cape Town, South Africa. He said Nigeria needed to invest more deliberately in specialised healthcare facilities capable of delivering advanced treatment and life-saving interventions for children. The proposed hospital in Ideato is expected to serve children from Imo State, the South-East and other parts of the country, subject to its eventual capacity and service arrangements. The bill was passed for second reading following a voice vote by the Deputy Speaker and referred to the relevant committee for further legislative consideration The post Reps pass bill for National Children’s Hospital in Imo appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: IPOB member pleads guilty, jailed 20 years for belonging to proscribed group
item.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA – The Federal High Court in Abuja, on Thursday, convicted and sentenced a self-confessed member of the Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB), Mr. Paul Okechukwu, 48, to 20 years in prison for belonging to a proscribed organisation. The defendant pleaded guilty to one count of a two-count charge the Federal Government preferred against him. The Federal Government alleged in the first count that the defendant, who is from Nnewi South in Anambra State, had in 2021, while in Imo State, committed an offence by belonging to IPOB, a proscribed organisation, contrary to and punishable under Section 16 of the Terrorism (Prevention) (Amendment) Act, 2013. In the second count, the Federal Government alleged that the defendant participated in an attack in which two security operatives were killed, and thereby committed an offence contrary to Section 2(1) of the Terrorism (Prevention) (Amendment) Act, 2013. After the charge was read to him, the defendant pleaded not guilty to the second count. In view of this development, and following an application by the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Prince Lateef Fagbemi, SAN, who was in court to lead the prosecution, the court struck out the second count after it was withdrawn. Relying on Section 72 of the Terrorism Prevention and Prohibition Act (TPPA) 2022, the Attorney-General applied for the court to allow a witness from the Department of State Services (DSS) to review some facts of the case. The witness, whose name was given as “ABC” for the purpose of the trial, identified the defendant as a member of IPOB, which he said had since been outlawed. He told the court that the defendant was involved in acts of terrorism, which he said included attacks on security agents. The witness, who said he was part of a team that investigated the defendant, tendered a copy of the report, which was admitted as Exhibit A. While applying for the defendant to be convicted, the AGF argued that the law prescribed a minimum sentence of 20 years for the offence. “We therefore urge my lord to impose the maximum sentence, at least to serve as a deterrent to others and to also show that the nation cannot condone any act of terrorism,” the AGF added. Meanwhile, immediately after the AGF made the application, the defendant broke down in tears in the dock, begging the court to temper justice with mercy. Delivering judgment in the matter, Justice Hawa Yilwa found the defendant guilty and sentenced him to 20 years. The court said it took note of the charge against the defendant and “the ripple effect it has on the nation.” It held that the defendant should be remanded in any correctional facility chosen by the Comptroller-General of the Nigerian Correctional Service to serve his sentence, which should count from the day he was arrested. The court held that the convict should be rehabilitated and redecalised upon the completion of his prison sentence. The post IPOB member pleads guilty, jailed

item.title: Nick Wright just doubled down on his ‘phenomenal’ Angel Reese take after watching WNBA Finals Game 3
item.description: Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Nick Wright has been left impressed with what he has seen from Angel Reese during the 2026 WNBA Finals so far. After Game 3, which took place on Wednesday, Reese became the first player in league history to drop three consecutive triple-doubles in her first three Finals games and is the youngest player in WNBA Finals history to record three straight double-doubles. Meanwhile, Nick Wright said ahead of Wednesday’s action that Reese has been phenomenal this year and her performances this postseason are giving her the opportunity to be one of the league’s best players behind A’ja Wilson. Prior to Game 3, Wright said: “If Angel Reese was going to have her status as a player stay at the level of her status as a celebrity, she needed to get better. It felt like her game had stagnated, if not dipped. Well, this year, that changed considerably; she’s been phenomenal. “Angel Reese’s performances these playoffs, as she might have her team on the doorstep of a championship, give her the opportunity to be right alongside, I’ll call it a step behind, A’ja Wilson as the top player in the sport.” Now, after the Atlanta Dream’s latest win, he has taken to X to quote the video of himself saying the above. He doubled down on his praise, listing off her impressive resume, describing it as a ‘Helluva portfolio’ while saying she is one game away from being the 2026 WNBA Finals MVP. He wrote: “Angel Reese is one game away from adding a Finals MVP trophy to go alongside her DPOY trophy, college National Championship trophy, NCAA Tournament MOP trophy. Helluva portfolio.” The Dream won Game 3 97-71, with Reese leading the game in scoring (21 points). Read more: ‘Is this political?’ – Enes Kanter demands meeting with Adam Silver over WNBA WNBA analyst sends message to Enes Kanter amid Game 3 attendance issue ‘Nothing but amazing…’ – Kara Lawson makes Angel Reese admission after Team USA experience

item.title: Big Ten Preview: Week 8
item.description: ANN ARBOR, MICHIGAN - OCTOBER 17: Tommy Carr #14 of the Michigan Wolverines runs the ball in for a touchdown past Kooper Ebel #8 and Alexander McPherson #33 of the Penn State Nittany Lions during the second half of a college football game at Michigan Stadium on October 17, 2026 in Ann Arbor, Michigan. The Michigan Wolverines won the game 21-18. (Photo by Aaron J. Thornton/Getty Images) | Getty Images While Penn State, and a number of other Big Ten programs take the week off, your Saturday will still be filled with conference action. Here are those games and what’s worth watching. SATURDAY AFTERNOON No. 6 Indiana (6-1, 3-1) at Michigan (4-2, 1-2), 12 p.m. on FOX Details : How does Indiana rebound after its first loss since December 2024? Meanwhile, how will Tommy Carr handle a Hoosier defense that will have spent the week getting ready for the first-year quarterback? Those are some of the questions that will be answered Saturday in Ann Arbor. Michigan’s defense is salty and figures to be a challenge for the sometimes erratic Josh Hoover. But Indiana hasn’t lost back-to-back games since Curt Cignetti arrived in Bloomington. Line : IU -7, Total 41.5 Should I watch this one : If you’re still in the mood to watch college football this weekend, this is the conference’s “biggest” game of the weekend. Rutgers (2-4, 1-2) at No. 25 Northwestern (5-1, 2-1), 12 p.m. on Peacock Details : Last weekend, the Scarlet Knights won a conference game and ended the Maryland career of Mike Locksley. Things will be more difficult for Greg Schiano’s bunch this weekend. Northwestern remains one of the big surprises of the Big Ten and they’ve been dominant at home – between two different stadiums even. The Wildcats’ ground game should have success, but don’t be shocked if KJ Duff and company make this one interesting despite the huge line. Line : NW -16.5, Total 58.5 Should I watch this one : I am wrong about a lot of things, but I think this game is worth keeping an eye on – if you’re still in the mood to watch college football. SATURDAY LATE AFTERNOON Oregon (4-2, 2-1) at Illinois (3-3, 1-2), 3 p.m. on BTN Details : Feels like a crossroads kind of game for two teams that have only been consistent in their inconsistencies. The Ducks are a solid road favorite, but their offense looked pedestrian at home last week in a win against Nebraska. The good news for Oregon is that the Illini defense is certainly not exactly a force. Oregon is a solid road favorite and a win here would at least put them back in the “we’re playing for something bigger” lane. But, a loss here and the Penn State 2025 comparisons heighten that much more. Line : NW -16.5, Total 58.5 Should I watch this one : I am wrong about a lot of things, but I think this game is worth keeping an eye on – if you’re still in the mood to watch college football. SATURDAY LATE AFTERNOON Oregon (4-2, 2-1) at Illinois (3-3, 1-2), 3 p.m. on BTN Details : Feels like a crossroads kind of game for two teams that have only been consistent in their inconsistencies. The good news for Oregon is that the Illini defense is certainly not exactly a force. Oregon is a solid road favorite and a win here would at least put them back in the “we’re playing for something bigger” lane. But, a loss here and the Penn State 2025 comparisons heighten that much more. Line : ORE -8.5, Total 50.5 Should I watch this one : This feels like a put it on the Quad Box kind of game until the fourth quarter. Michigan State (2-5, 0-4) at No. 9 UCLA (6-0, 4-0), 3:30 p.m. on CBS Details : The lone unbeaten team in the Big Ten is at home for a showcase game. UCLA only has a single game left on its schedule against a team that is currently ranked and the Bruins seem to be doing exactly what Indiana did back in 2024: taking full advantage of a softer schedule and poising itself for a playoff appearance with a former JMU coach. Michigan State is coming off back-to-back heartbreaking home losses. What do the Spartans have in reserve for the road trip out west? Line : UCLA -14.5, Total 43.5 Should I watch this one : I am sure there’s some curiosity around these parts about what Bob Chesney is doing, but otherwise I would just check in periodically. No. 15 Iowa (5-1, 2-1) at Minnesota (4-2, 2-1), 3:30 p.m. on FS1 Details : The Gophers have been one of the league’s more curious teams: they have a quarterback that a lot of people like, they play hard for PJ Fleck, they celebrated like crazy when they beat Michigan at home for the first time since the 1970s. They’ve also been flattened at home by Mississippi State and they were trounced at Purdue. Iowa remains the consistent Iowa as always. So, what version of Minnesota shows up in this one seems to be the biggest question. A Hawkeye win here and the playoff talk can get serious. Line : Iowa -6.5, Total 40.5 Should I watch this one : This is at least a Quad Box game with this week’s slate. SATURDAY EVENING No. 16 USC (6-1, 3-1) at Wisconsin (4-2, 2-1), 7:30 p.m. on NBC Details : Lincoln Riley’s team still has the label of struggling on the road in conference play, especially when heading east out of Los Angeles. Well, the Trojans are 2-0 away from the friendly confines this year, including the 31-23 win in the Whiteout. This feels like a similar kind of game. Wisconsin will probably move the ball on USC, since everyone does. But, who can win the red zone battle? Both teams did against Penn State – and that’s why both knocked off the Nittany Lions. That figures to be a key in this one. Line : USC -3, Total 50.5 Should I watch this one : Still feeling it on Saturday night, put this one on the big screen as you turn the page on another week of conference action.

item.title: Can Wisconsin upset USC this weekend?
item.description: PASADENA, CA - OCTOBER 17: Wisconsin Badgers head coach Luke Fickell during the game between the UCLA Bruins and the Wisconsin Badgers on October 17, 2026 at Rose Bowl Stadium in Pasadena. (Photo by David Dennis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NCAA. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Wisconsin fans and fans across the country. Coming off a 17-7 loss to the UCLA Bruins, the Wisconsin Badgers will have to bounce back quickly against another West Coast team, as they take on the USC Trojans at Camp Randall Stadium this weekend. Coming into the game, the Badgers are 2.5-point underdogs at home, facing a Trojans team with an explosive offense that has gone 6-1 thus far. However, many of USC’s wins to date have been uninspiring. They’re on a two-game win streak following their loss to Oregon, but they’ve played two disappointing teams in Washington and Penn State quite closely (25-21 and 31-23). Apart from that, they also had a close 42-35 win over Rutgers and a few early-season wins where they won more comfortably, but the defense was exposed as a problem in the second half. Despite switching coordinators, the Trojans continue to have problems defensively, and Lincoln Riley has been on many hot seat lists, even with his supposed $70+ million buyout. So this game is huge for both sides: the Badgers need a win to get back on the right track, while the Trojans can’t afford a loss in their hope of a College Football Playoff appearance. Does Wisconsin have what it takes to pull off the upset here in Week 6? Let us know by voting in our weekly Reacts poll below and sharing your thoughts in the comments! item.title: Luis Díaz suffers muscle tear and is sidelined for now
item.description: Luis Díaz suffers muscle tear and is sidelined for now Bad news for FC Bayern Munich. Colombian forward Luis Díaz suffered a minor tear in his left hamstring during the Champions League match against Arsenal. The injury was confirmed by the club's medical department after the player underwent the necessary tests. The 29-year-old will be sidelined until further notice. The coach and Bayern fans will temporarily be without a key player in the team's attacking setup, right at a demanding stage of the season. item.title: 2026-27 Ivy League Men’s Basketball Preview
item.description: ALLSTON, MA - OCTOBER 14: A close up view of the Ivy League logo on a basketball during Harvard Crimson Madness on October 14, 2022, at Lavietes Pavilion in Allston, MA. (Photo by Erica Denhoff/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images After years of the same eight coaches, there have been five coaching changes in the last three seasons of Ivy League basketball. Fran McCaffery made waves by winning Ivy Madness in year one at Penn last season. Can the Quakers go back-to-back? Harvard and Yale have vengeance on their minds after overtime losses to the Quakers in Ithaca. Princeton returns its entire team. Cornell looks to get over the hump, while Columbia, Dartmouth and Brown look for breakthroughs under their second- and first-year coaches. 1. PENN WHAT I LIKE: The Quakers return most of their rotation pieces from the squad that shocked the world and won Ivy Madness last year. That all starts with TJ Power, whose 44-point miracle performance against Yale stands as one of the league’s greatest ever. He’s a legit three-level scoring superstar in the Ivy League, and at 6-foot-8, he’s a mismatch nightmare for opponents. One of the league’s deadliest shooters, Mike Zanoni, returns alongside him. Notre Dame transfer Sir Mohammed adds a little bit of physicality on the wing, something that Penn desperately needs. There’s depth in the frontcourt with the returning Dalton Scantlebury/Augie Gerhart duo. Both are skilled post scorers, and I think Scantlebury could eventually leapfrog Gerhart in the rotation. Lucas Lueth also gives the Quakers some rim protection and athleticism up front, although he’s more a four than five. WHAT I DON’T LIKE: Penn’s analytical profile relies a ton on mid-range jump shots. The Quakers didn’t get to the rim at a high enough rate last year and are one of the few teams that still consistently runs actions for long twos. Penn will have the same strengths and weaknesses as last season. That might be a good thing, because they won the Ivy League, but by virtue of winning the league through miraculous measures, it may have raised the expectations higher than they should be. Penn will be out to prove that it didn’t merely catch lightning in a bottle in Ithaca. X-FACTOR: AJ Levine. What is the ceiling for AJ Levine? He’s already one of the best guards in the Ivy League on the defensive end, but without Ethan Roberts, he’ll have to shoulder a bigger role on offense. Can he step up as a scorer to give another element to this group? 2. YALE WHAT I LIKE: James Jones has never really needed to rebuild since COVID. He’s always found his next star waiting in the wings. Trevor Mullin and Riley Fox are the obvious candidates this season. Mullin started at the point for the Bulldogs last year and is an efficient outside shooter who doesn’t turn the ball over much. He’ll need to take a big step forward though. Fox is arguably the Ivy League’s best shooter. The 6-foot-6 sniper shot 37% on four attempts per game last year
item.content:encoded: ALLSTON, MA - OCTOBER 14: A close up view of the Ivy League logo on a basketball during Harvard Crimson Madness on October 14, 2022, at Lavietes Pavilion in Allston, MA. (Photo by Erica Denhoff/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images After years of the same eight coaches, there have been five coaching changes in the last three seasons of Ivy League basketball. Fran McCaffery made waves by winning Ivy Madness in year one at Penn last season. Can the Quakers go back-to-back? Harvard and Yale have vengeance on their minds after overtime losses to the Quakers in Ithaca. Princeton returns its entire team. Cornell looks to get over the hump, while Columbia, Dartmouth and Brown look for breakthroughs under their second- and first-year coaches. 1. PENN WHAT I LIKE: The Quakers return most of their rotation pieces from the squad that shocked the world and won Ivy Madness last year. That all starts with TJ Power, whose 44-point miracle performance against Yale stands as one of the league’s greatest ever. He’s a legit three-level scoring superstar in the Ivy League, and at 6-foot-8, he’s a mismatch nightmare for opponents. One of the league’s deadliest shooters, Mike Zanoni, returns alongside him. Notre Dame transfer Sir Mohammed adds a little bit of physicality on the wing, something that Penn desperately needs. There’s depth in the frontcourt with the returning Dalton Scantlebury/Augie Gerhart duo. Both are skilled post scorers, and I think Scantlebury could eventually leapfrog Gerhart in the rotation. Lucas Lueth also gives the Quakers some rim protection and athleticism up front, although he’s more a four than five. WHAT I DON’T LIKE: Penn’s analytical profile relies a ton on mid-range jump shots. The Quakers didn’t get to the rim at a high enough rate last year and are one of the few teams that still consistently runs actions for long twos. Penn will have the same strengths and weaknesses as last season. That might be a good thing, because they won the Ivy League, but by virtue of winning the league through miraculous measures, it may have raised the expectations higher than they should be. Penn will be out to prove that it didn’t merely catch lightning in a bottle in Ithaca. X-FACTOR: AJ Levine. What is the ceiling for AJ Levine? He’s already one of the best guards in the Ivy League on the defensive end, but without Ethan Roberts, he’ll have to shoulder a bigger role on offense. Can he step up as a scorer to give another element to this group? 2. YALE WHAT I LIKE: James Jones has never really needed to rebuild since COVID. He’s always found his next star waiting in the wings. Trevor Mullin and Riley Fox are the obvious candidates this season. Mullin started at the point for the Bulldogs last year and is an efficient outside shooter who doesn’t turn the ball over much. He’ll need to take a big step forward though. Fox is arguably the Ivy League’s best shooter. The 6-foot-6 sniper shot 37% on four attempts per game last year and will probably take way more than that this season. Jordan Brathwaite also is back, another stellar shooter who will make this one of the most dynamic shooting teams in the league. WHAT I DON’T LIKE: Despite those two players, this is probably the weakest Yale returning crop in some time. After losing Samson Aletan a year early and Isaac Celiscar two years early, the Buldogs are relying on a lot of players who haven’t proven anything at all. Courtney Wallace and Daniel Ogunyemi have potential but haven’t shown much. Wallace’s athleticism could be a major piece for a backcourt that lacks the level of athleticism that it has had over the past few years. Division-III transfer Connor May will also play a role with his shooting. X-FACTOR: Jack Sullivan. Yale has not finished outside the top 2 in defense in the Ivy League since before COVID. If the Bulldogs do it again, Sullivan must be an excellent rim protector. The 6-foot-11 sophomore didn’t play much last year, but the keys to the season are in his hands. 3. HARVARD WHAT I LIKE: The returning trio of Rob Hinton, Tey Barbour and Thomas Batties II is the best in the Ivy League. Hinton is arguably the most talented player in the conference as a 6-foot-5 jumbo creator that gets to his spots and scores at a high level. He must take a step forward as a playmaker and shooter this year, but the talent is there. Barbour and Batties were knockdown shooters last season, while Batties provided interior rim protection. Ben Eisendrath was a pesky player off the ball, and a healthy Austin Hunt could make a big difference as well. WHAT I DON’T LIKE: I don’t think people talked enough about how much Chandler Piggé did for the Crimson last year. He was the glue guy on both ends who made that team work. Perhaps Hunt can bring some of that back without Piggé this year. Additionally, it’s harder to trust Tommy Amaker than it was 10 years ago. A coaching gap might be the difference between the Crimson and the two teams above them. With the same strengths and weaknesses as last year, unless Harvard finds more production outside of its stars, it could limit the ceiling. X-FACTOR: Freshman class. The Crimson once again have a loaded freshman group. Jason Singleton and Preston Merrick are athletic players who can impact the game by pushing the pace for Harvard, an element that the team didn’t have last year. Singleton seems like the most important piece, as a highly-touted combo guard with scoring chops. Merrick is more of an off-ball runner type. Listen to Ivy men’s conference preview podcast episode: View Link Listen to Ivy women’s conference preview podcast episode: View Link 4. PRINCETON WHAT I LIKE: Princeton returns the entire rotation from last season. When you run a Princeton-style offense, continuity and familiarity is extremely important. It’s not just the starting group. It’s everybody. Jack Stanton, Malik Abdullahi and CJ Happy are now upperclassmen. Dalen Davis, Jackson Hicke and Jacob Huggins are seniors. They’ve all been through the battles in this system. They’ve all had their bouts with inconsistency but have shown the ability to be the guy on a given night. Stanton returning from injury after missing the final stretch of the season will be a huge boon to the offense as he’s an elite shooter. Hicke took a huge step last year as well. I really liked what Landon Clark gave the Tigers last season, and as a sophomore, he could be a key glue guy. WHAT I DON’T LIKE: Last year was the worst Princeton team that Mitch Henderson fielded as Tiger head coach. They finished with a losing Ivy record for the second time in his tenure and failed to crack double-digit wins for the first time since 2007-08. As I’ve said with Penn and Harvard, when you retain as much, you don’t just retain the strengths, but also the weaknesses. There aren’t a lot of great individual defenders on this roster, and Princeton was the worst defensive rebounding team in the Ivy League last year, which is a far cry from a program strength. X-FACTOR: Dalen Davis is Princeton’s most talented offensive player. He needs to be consistent on that end this year. The Tigers will not be able to afford sinking 30% usage rates into him if he’s putting up a 99.2 offensive rating again this year. He doesn’t have to be the best player on the floor every night, but he has to be able to pick and choose his spots. 5. CORNELL WHAT I LIKE: The backcourt has a lot of fun pieces. Jacob Beccles is in line to be Cornell’s next All-Ivy guard as a senior. Each year, he’s gotten more decisive and aggressive and provides positional size and physicality to score inside and out. Anthony Nimani is also poised for a big season with a bigger role, while Mateen Rafiq might be the biggest upside piece for the Big Red as he sees more playing time. Transfers JJ Sanchez and Luke Kennevan can add serious shooting potential as well. Mikehi Williams, 6-foot-6 freshman wing, can be an impact player in year one. WHAT I DON’T LIKE:

item.title: ‘I lost all respect’: Rookie calls out Luka Doncic for ‘whining and complaining’
item.description: Mar 27, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Lakers guard Luka Doncic (77) gestures during the second half against the Brooklyn Nets at Crypto.com Arena. Mandatory Credit: William Liang-Imagn Images Yaxel Lendeborg’s NBA debut didn’t go the way he wanted, as the Golden State Warriors were blown out by the Los Angeles Lakers on opening night. But the rookie certainly made sure that people would be talking about him afterward. Lendeborg spent much of Wednesday’s game going back and forth with Lakers star Luka Doncic, and he picked up a technical foul in the process. Afterward, he didn’t hold back, saying that he “lost all respect” for Doncic because of the way he begs for foul calls. Heated Debut With Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody out injured, the Warriors started Lendeborg on the wing and had him guard Doncic for much of the game. He held his own, holding Doncic to 1-of-6 shooting as the primary defender, according to Anthony Slater of ESPN . But the Lakers still rolled to a 127-105 win, building a lead as large as 35 points. Doncic finished with 28 points. Things got heated late in the second quarter, when Doncic pump-faked Lendeborg into a shooting foul and let him know about it. The two kept jawing at each other, and Lendeborg was eventually hit with a technical foul. Doncic got the last laugh at the end of the first half, banking in a 48-foot heave at the buzzer and then pointing and laughing at Lendeborg. “He kind of lured him in a little bit,” Warriors coach Steve Kerr said. “I thought the single technical was ridiculous. They were jawing at each other. I think it was the words Yaxel used that got him the T. But then Luka makes the half-court shot and gets in his face. That should be a tech.” ‘I Lost All Respect’ Lendeborg, who finished with 12 points in 29 minutes, made it clear after the game that he wasn’t impressed with Doncic. And a clip of his comments quickly went viral. “I had a lot of respect for him [because] I didn’t really watch the NBA much,” Lendeborg said, via ESPN. “I just watched highlights and seen him kill people. But being in it firsthand and seeing all the whining and complaining, I lost all respect.” “That was awful,” Lendeborg continued. “Me getting frustrated, it’s not about the foul being called, it’s about him complaining the entire game.” “You get the foul call. Congratulations, bro,” he added. “Then you talk to me like you did something great. C’mon, dog. That [stuff] is weak. It kind of threw me off because I have so much respect for him. Gone, man. Gone.” Lendeborg also admitted that he spent the whole game letting Doncic hear about it. “I was telling him he sucks,” Lendeborg said. “He can’t score on me. You talk but you can’t score on me. I said it the whole game. I said a couple cuss words, obviously. That’s why I got the technical. item.title: Champions League review: PSG take a hit, Man City’s empty seats and teenage hope for Liverpool
item.description: The reigning champions must deal with the absence of Khvicha Kvaratskhelia for some time, while fans at Anfield were thrilled by Rio Ngumoha Paris Saint-Germain beat Barcelona 4-2 on Tuesday , but the reigning champions lost the best player in last season’s tournament, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia. This autumn has seen much lobbying for the Ballon d’Or, with the Georgian a popular choice, despite his absence from the World Cup. He is expected to be out for six months, although Rodri’s comeback from serious injury – he was rested by Barcelona on Tuesday until coming off the bench in the 60th minute – shows it can take far longer than that for players to rediscover their highest level. Continue reading...

item.title: 5 questions with a Bears expert: How is Caleb Williams looking?
item.description: Led by second-year head coaches and first-round quarterbacks drafted in 2024, and owning identical 4-2 records, the New England Patriots and Chicago Bears are quite similar to one another. On Thursday night, they will share the field for a prime time matchup — the second between the two clubs in the last three years. To find out more about the Patriots’ opponent, we spoke with Bill Zimmerman of Pats Pulpit’s sister site Windy City Gridiron , the SB Nation community for all things Bears. 1. I know it’s a small sample size, but how has Caleb Williams looked in his second season under Ben Johnson? What changed in his return to the field from when Tyler Bagent was under center? Without trying to sound too much like a raging homer, Caleb has looked fantastic in year two. If you don’t consider the week two loss to the Vikings, where Caleb got hurt due to significantly wet and sloppy conditions (it didn’t just rain; it was a monsoon), the offense has looked like arguably the best in the league. Mind you, that’s only two games, so it’s not enough to go on, but it’s been that good in the small sample size. With Case Keenum and Tyson Bagent, the Bears averaged 19 points per game. With Caleb Williams, they’ve averaged 45 PPG in his two full games. Williams is getting to the point where he can stay in the pocket, operate the Ben Johnson system quickly and efficiently, and keep the chains moving. But Caleb also has the ability to break out of the system and ad-lib on his own, where he gets really dangerous and makes many of the huge off-script plays that make all the highlight reels. Bagent doesn’t have the ability to operate off-script, and he also doesn’t have a strong arm. Bagent needs to operate quickly, and if he doesn’t get the ball out on time, he can’t make up for it either with his arm and ability to operate if the play breaks down. Caleb is the exact opposite. He can be late on a read but make up for it with insane release and arm strength. With Caleb back and (mostly) healthy, it’s a dangerous two-headed weapon. First, it’s Ben Johnson’s offense and play calling, which everyone in the league knows is elite. But if the play Johnson calls doesn’t have it, the defense still has to deal with what Caleb Williams can do when the play breaks down. The Bears offense has a chance to really hit some great heights this year with the synergy that Ben and Caleb are developing. 2. How will not having Kyle Monangai affect the Bears’ offense? Who would be the next men up? Monangai missing is definitely a knock to the offense. He and D’Andre Swift make a great combination, and they complement each other well. Roschon Johnson would be the guy to fill in. Johnson doesn’t have the speed or shiftiness of Monangai. There are fans I know that call him SlowJo instead of RoJo. item.content:encoded: Led by second-year head coaches and first-round quarterbacks drafted in 2024, and owning identical 4-2 records, the New England Patriots and Chicago Bears are quite similar to one another. On Thursday night, they will share the field for a prime time matchup — the second between the two clubs in the last three years. To find out more about the Patriots’ opponent, we spoke with Bill Zimmerman of Pats Pulpit’s sister site Windy City Gridiron , the SB Nation community for all things Bears. 1. I know it’s a small sample size, but how has Caleb Williams looked in his second season under Ben Johnson? What changed in his return to the field from when Tyler Bagent was under center? Without trying to sound too much like a raging homer, Caleb has looked fantastic in year two. If you don’t consider the week two loss to the Vikings, where Caleb got hurt due to significantly wet and sloppy conditions (it didn’t just rain; it was a monsoon), the offense has looked like arguably the best in the league. Mind you, that’s only two games, so it’s not enough to go on, but it’s been that good in the small sample size. With Case Keenum and Tyson Bagent, the Bears averaged 19 points per game. With Caleb Williams, they’ve averaged 45 PPG in his two full games. Williams is getting to the point where he can stay in the pocket, operate the Ben Johnson system quickly and efficiently, and keep the chains moving. But Caleb also has the ability to break out of the system and ad-lib on his own, where he gets really dangerous and makes many of the huge off-script plays that make all the highlight reels. Bagent doesn’t have the ability to operate off-script, and he also doesn’t have a strong arm. Bagent needs to operate quickly, and if he doesn’t get the ball out on time, he can’t make up for it either with his arm and ability to operate if the play breaks down. Caleb is the exact opposite. He can be late on a read but make up for it with insane release and arm strength. With Caleb back and (mostly) healthy, it’s a dangerous two-headed weapon. First, it’s Ben Johnson’s offense and play calling, which everyone in the league knows is elite. But if the play Johnson calls doesn’t have it, the defense still has to deal with what Caleb Williams can do when the play breaks down. The Bears offense has a chance to really hit some great heights this year with the synergy that Ben and Caleb are developing. 2. How will not having Kyle Monangai affect the Bears’ offense? Who would be the next men up? Monangai missing is definitely a knock to the offense. He and D’Andre Swift make a great combination, and they complement each other well. Roschon Johnson would be the guy to fill in. Johnson doesn’t have the speed or shiftiness of Monangai. There are fans I know that call him SlowJo instead of RoJo. He had just 6 yards on five attempts against Green Bay, and last week he was much better with 51 yards on 13 carries, but that still keeps him below the 4.0 threshold. Johnson is a nice blocker, has pretty good hands, and is a good special teamer. But he’s not a guy you want having 10-plus touches in a game. 3. The Bears have been one of the league’s worst deep pass defenses, but their corners seem to be getting healthy. What’s behind those struggles and how much would having all three starters affect Chicago’s ability to defend deep? What’s behind the Bears’ lack of success from their secondary? I mean, should I say lack of talent? With Kyler Gordon out, the Bears were mostly running out Jaylon Johnson, Tyrique Stevenson, and rookie Malik Muhammad. With Gordon back last week, they have moved Muhammad to play more outside and made them less reliant on the other two. Reports were really good over the summer that Johnson had recovered from the injuries that plagued him in 2025, and he was back to his old form. That really hasn’t been the case. He’s made occasional plays but has largely looked like a player that may have lost some athleticism and isn’t able to keep up with faster receivers stretching the field. Stevenson can make plays as well because he’s a pretty aggressive corner. However, Stevenson, between being overly aggressive and lapses in concentration, consistently gets burned on deep balls as well. Having Gordon back gives them a great blitzing weapon and great play at the line of scrimmage, and his presence will limit how much someone like Stevenson has to be on the field. That will help in some regards, but the Bears are going to be susceptible to the deep ball against Drake Maye for sure. 4. What’s makes the Bears such an effective blitzing defense? Has anyone managed to slow them down? The key to the Bears blitzing is the success they are having with it on third down. The Bears have 17 sacks on the season; nine of them have come on third down. That makes them arguably the best third-down defense in the NFL. Heading into this game, opponents have converted just 26% of their third downs against the Bears, trailing only the Minnesota Vikings. Defensive Coordinator Dennis Allen has been a wizard with this team on third downs, and that’s not just last year; they were good on third downs last year as well, despite being one of the worst overall defenses in the league. What’s wild about those nine third-down sacks I mentioned earlier, four have come from defensive backs. You can expect Kyler Gordon to blitz frequently, and with the banged-up Patriots offensive line, it wouldn’t shock me if he gets home for another sack on Thursday night. Even in the Bears’ losses, the third-down conversion rates sit at 7-for-25, so still close to their averages. It sounds dumb, but the best way to beat the Bears’ third-down success? Stay out of third and long. The Bears can be had on first and second down, so gain yards there, avoid third downs all together or at least keep it to third and short where it’s a quick-hitting play and the blitz doesn’t have a chance to get home. 5. Who do you think pulls out a victory on Thursday night, and why? I do think the Bears are going to win this one. I think they are carrying a lot of momentum and confidence with Caleb Williams back. I think the offense is clicking, and I do think the Patriots’ defense can cause some issues for them, but I do think they can score on them. I expect Drake Maye to beat the Bears with a few pretty deep balls, but I do think they will make some plays on third down and stop enough Patriots drives. Thursday games are tricky because they always seem like anything can happen with a short week of preparation. These are two good football teams, so we should expect a close game. Bears 27, Patriots 24.

item.title: How to get electronic sensors in DMZ in Modern Warfare 4
item.description: Every single player will need to find electronic sensors in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's DMZ mode, because they're an essential resource early on. item.title: Dortmund U19s fired up for another derby win
item.description: Dortmund U19s fired up for another derby win Youth fixtures at a glance U23: BVB – Bonner SC (Regionalliga West): 23 October 2026, 19:30 (Stadion Rote Erde) FC Schalke 04 – BVB (DFB Youth League): 25 October 2026, 11:00 (Parkstadion, Parkallee 3, Gelsenkirchen) U23s hoping to keep their impressive run going Thanks to four consecutive wins, Borussia have now drawn level on points with league leaders Oberhausen. They are therefore increasingly being tipped as promotion contenders. “Nobody named us as the outright favourites before the season. I see it the same way. But the lads have developed – and we’ll carry that progress forward,” says BVB head coach Daniel Rios in response to questions on the subject. In their home match against Bonner SC, the only unbeaten team in the Regionalliga West will be looking to extend their winning run. The task is unlikely to be easy, however. Seventh-placed Bonn arrive having put together an impressive run of their own until last weekend. The “Rhine Lions” had gone ten games unbeaten before a 1-0 home defeat to Hilden brought that streak to an end. Rios approaches the match with respect: “Bonn have shown in recent weeks how difficult they are to beat. They have players who can make the difference in the Regionalliga on a good day. They also have a clear plan – both in and out of possession.” It remains to be seen whether BVB will have a full squad to choose from. U23 players Aaron Held, Tim Degener and Fadi Zarqelain only returned on Wednesday from the U19s’ Youth League match in Baku. A late decision will be made on whether they feature in the starting line-up. Midfielder Mussa Kaba remains unavailable with a shoulder injury. Tickets for the match are available from the BVB online ticket shop , and the game will also be broadcast live on LEAGUES . Excitement banishes fatigue: U19s fired up for the Revierderby Three games, three wins: coach Felix Hirschnagl’s team have handled an intense run of fixtures with impressive composure. A resounding 5-0 victory away to Norwegian Youth League side FK Bodø/Glimt was followed by a 6-2 home win over Rot-Weiß Oberhausen. Most recently, BVB also won 2-0 away to Sabah FC in Azerbaijan. In just seven days, Borussia have built up plenty of confidence for their next demanding challenge: the prestigious Revierderby away to FC Schalke 04 on Sunday (11:00). Dortmund will be looking for another victory to retain their lead at the top of the DFB Youth League. The special significance of this historic rivalry should help them quickly put the exertions of two long away trips behind them. “We know how difficult it is to play in the Youth League after a UEFA Youth League match. We’ve now travelled around 11,000 kilometres, so we’ll recover and then focus fully on the derby,” explains Hirschnagl. There is every indication that this will be an evenly matched contest.
