They are therefore increasingly being tipped as promotion contenders. “Nobody named us as the outright favourites before the season. I see it the same way. But the lads have developed – and we’ll carry that progress forward,” says BVB head coach Daniel Rios in response to questions on the subject. In their home match against Bonner SC, the only unbeaten team in the Regionalliga West will be looking to extend their winning run. The task is unlikely to be easy, however. Seventh-placed Bonn arrive having put together an impressive run of their own until last weekend. The “Rhine Lions” had gone ten games unbeaten before a 1-0 home defeat to Hilden brought that streak to an end. U23 players Aaron Held, Tim Degener and Fadi Zarqelain only returned on Wednesday from the U19s’ Youth League match in Baku. A late decision will be made on whether they feature in the starting line-up. Midfielder Mussa Kaba remains unavailable with a shoulder injury. Tickets for the match are available from the BVB online ticket shop , and the game will also be broadcast live on LEAGUES . Excitement banishes fatigue: U19s fired up for the Revierderby Three games, three wins: coach Felix Hirschnagl’s team have handled an intense run of fixtures with impressive composure. A resounding 5-0 victory away to Norwegian Youth League side FK Bodø/Glimt was followed by a 6-2 home win over Rot-Weiß Oberhausen. Most recently, BVB also won 2-0 away to Sabah FC in Azerbaijan. In just seven days, Borussia have built up plenty of confidence for their next demanding challenge: the prestigious Revierderby away to FC Schalke 04 on Sunday (11:00). Dortmund will be looking for another victory to retain their lead at the top of the DFB Youth League. The special significance of this historic rivalry should help them quickly put the exertions of two long away trips behind them. “We know how difficult it is to play in the Youth League after a UEFA Youth League match. We’ve now travelled around 11,000 kilometres, so we’ll recover and then focus fully on the derby,” explains Hirschnagl. There is every indication that this will be an evenly matched contest. The reverse fixture was fiercely contested and decided by an early Schalke own goal. BVB narrowly won 1-0, so the hosts are likely to be out for revenge. “They’ll want to get their own back for that,” warns Hirschnagl. The league standings add extra spice to the derby. Fourth-placed Schalke are already eight points behind Borussia and are under pressure. The Royal Blues urgently need points to avoid further jeopardising their chances of qualifying for the main round. Hirschnagl therefore expects opponents who will throw everything into the game: “I’ve looked at the table. This is pretty much their last chance to reach the main round. Unlike the U19s, however, they still have a few days to wait for their encounter. Their matchday ten fixture against MSV Duisburg, brought forward and won 4-1 by BVB last Wednesday, gives coach Karsten Gorges’ team a free weekend. The extra time is welcome, allowing Dortmund to prepare at their leisure for the eagerly awaited top-of-the-table clash at the Parkstadion on 30 October at 16:00. item.title: How to increase stash size in DMZ in Modern Warfare 4
item.description: One problem that everyone is going to encounter in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's DMZ mode is how to increase your stash size . item.title: PREVIEW | RB Leipzig vs SV 07 Elversberg: team news, lineups, predictions (Bundesliga 24/10)
item.description: PREVIEW | RB Leipzig vs SV 07 Elversberg: team news, lineups, predictions (Bundesliga 24/10) RB Leipzig and SV 07 Elversberg face off this Saturday at the Red Bull Arena in 1. Bundesliga . RB Leipzig have picked up 9 points and currently lie in 7th position. item.title: Steve Kerr caught on hot mic calling out Lakers double standards
item.description: Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images Steve Kerr didn’t realise his mic was still hot, but fans certainly heard him loud and clear as he vented his frustration over how refs whistle games in Los Angeles. The Golden State Warriors suffered a rough 127-105 blowout loss to the Los Angeles Lakers, with familiar officiating frustrations boiling over once again. Fans and players vented over Luka Doncic’s whistle advantage, calling out his constant foul-baiting and whining to the refs after every drive. The Lakers shot 24-of-27 from the free throw line on 25 personal fouls called against Golden State. Meanwhile, the Warriors shot 21-of-27 from the charity stripe on 19 fouls called against LA. Steve Kerr warns Yaxel Lendeborg about refereeing vs Lakers Steve Kerr didn’t realise the broadcast mics were picking up every word when he leaned in to talk to Yaxel Lendeborg on the sideline. Trailing by 22 in the third quarter, Kerr vented his frustration right into the mic, complaining about the soft whistle the Lakers were getting at home. Shown live on ESPN, Brick Center shared the video, where Kerr said: “They call all that s*** here, they wouldn’t call it in any other arena.” Kerr’s hot mic frustration matches what Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg experienced directly on the court. After guarding Luka Doncic, Lendeborg admitted he lost all respect for the star , calling out his non-stop flopping, whining to refs, and the soft calls that left Golden State defenseless. Read more: ‘No, not LeBron’: Shaquille O’Neal says 76ers ‘will not win’ if one player doesn’t perform Steph Curry has a message for Yaxel Lendeborg after Luka Doncic drama ‘Do you understand?’ – Stephen A. Smith reveals Donald Trump’s ‘greatest president’ claim

item.title: On this day: Fernando Alonso wins the world title, Michael Schumacher retires from F1
item.description: Motorsport photo On 22 October 2006, Fernando Alonso beat Michael Schumacher to the world title in the Brazilian Grand Prix, as the seven-time champion retired from Formula 1. In truth, there was little doubt Alonso was going to clinch a second crown that day. Schumacher’s engine failure and retirement from the lead of the Suzuka race had turned a potential two-point lead into a 10-point deficit, meaning the Ferrari racer needed both to win and his rival not to score at Interlagos. That endeavour took a turn for the worse when Schumacher encountered a fuel pressure problem in Q3, leaving him 10th on the grid with Alonso fourth. “I don't know what we can do,” the German said after qualifying. “I don't know how the race will develop. It is hard to predict something, but I will try my best. It is much more difficult starting from 10th, but of course I will try.” “Let's not forget that in the past, Michael has managed to win races starting even further back on the grid,” Ferrari technical director Ross Brawn added. That statement was inaccurate – across the preceding 248 races, Schumacher had won from outside the top 10 just once – but the Ferrari driver showed exactly why Brawn made it. He jumped from 10th to seventh on the first lap, then passed former team-mate Rubens Barrichello and overtook Giancarlo Fisichella around the outside for fifth on lap eight – meaning he was already right behind his title rival – but the slightest of touches with the Renault caused a rear-left puncture. Michael Schumacher, Ferrari Michael Schumacher, Ferrari Schumacher found himself down in 20th, 69 seconds adrift of race-leading team-mate Felipe Massa , while his deficit to Alonso was exactly one minute. By lap 27, he had caught the back of the pack and successively overtook Tiago Monteiro, Robert Doornbos, Nick Heidfeld and Robert Kubica , while undercutting other opponents and benefitting from retirements, to find himself fifth before his second pitstop. Emerging back out in seventh, Schumacher passed Barrichello again and pressured Fisichella into a lock-up in Turn 1 to claim fifth on lap 63. Massa’s commanding home drive meant he was still 33 seconds up the road, but second-placed Alonso was just eight seconds away from the recovering Ferrari. Schumacher ran out of laps to claim a podium finish but still performed a clinical move on McLaren ’s Kimi Raikkonen on the antepenultimate lap to take fourth position, as Alonso secured the championship. item.content:encoded: Motorsport photo On 22 October 2006, Fernando Alonso beat Michael Schumacher to the world title in the Brazilian Grand Prix, as the seven-time champion retired from Formula 1. In truth, there was little doubt Alonso was going to clinch a second crown that day. Schumacher’s engine failure and retirement from the lead of the Suzuka race had turned a potential two-point lead into a 10-point deficit, meaning the Ferrari racer needed both to win and his rival not to score at Interlagos. That endeavour took a turn for the worse when Schumacher encountered a fuel pressure problem in Q3, leaving him 10th on the grid with Alonso fourth. “I don't know what we can do,” the German said after qualifying. “I don't know how the race will develop. It is hard to predict something, but I will try my best. It is much more difficult starting from 10th, but of course I will try.” “Let's not forget that in the past, Michael has managed to win races starting even further back on the grid,” Ferrari technical director Ross Brawn added. That statement was inaccurate – across the preceding 248 races, Schumacher had won from outside the top 10 just once – but the Ferrari driver showed exactly why Brawn made it. He jumped from 10th to seventh on the first lap, then passed former team-mate Rubens Barrichello and overtook Giancarlo Fisichella around the outside for fifth on lap eight – meaning he was already right behind his title rival – but the slightest of touches with the Renault caused a rear-left puncture. Michael Schumacher, Ferrari Michael Schumacher, Ferrari Schumacher found himself down in 20th, 69 seconds adrift of race-leading team-mate Felipe Massa , while his deficit to Alonso was exactly one minute. By lap 27, he had caught the back of the pack and successively overtook Tiago Monteiro, Robert Doornbos, Nick Heidfeld and Robert Kubica , while undercutting other opponents and benefitting from retirements, to find himself fifth before his second pitstop. Emerging back out in seventh, Schumacher passed Barrichello again and pressured Fisichella into a lock-up in Turn 1 to claim fifth on lap 63. Massa’s commanding home drive meant he was still 33 seconds up the road, but second-placed Alonso was just eight seconds away from the recovering Ferrari. Schumacher ran out of laps to claim a podium finish but still performed a clinical move on McLaren ’s Kimi Raikkonen on the antepenultimate lap to take fourth position, as Alonso secured the championship. Fernando Alonso, Renault, Michael Schumacher, Ferrari Fernando Alonso, Renault, Michael Schumacher, Ferrari “The race was chaotic, I think that is the right word,” Schumacher said. “We really had a superb car today, from the pure speed we could have lapped everybody. So I have to say it was the perfect end to the season in terms of car performance, but for me it didn't work out well.” Alonso hailed a “fantastic way” to conclude his time at Renault, which he described as “my family in Formula 1”, ahead of his long-awaited move to McLaren for 2007. “I will have these memories with them all my life, and to finish the last race like this is something that you never dream of, you never even try to dream of, because it's always more than what you expected,” he commented. Fernando Alonso, Renault Fernando Alonso, Renault With that career path, the Spaniard dreamt of emulating Ayrton Senna . “To join McLaren and never to race with Ferrari reminds me a lot of Senna,” he told TV channel Telecinco. “He won three titles, and for me, to retire with three and achieve what he achieved would be the objective of my career.” Twenty years on, Alonso is still chasing that third crown in F1. Meanwhile, Schumacher looked back on his glittering career, one month after announcing his retirement in Monza . With Ferrari signing Raikkonen for 2007, Schumacher staying would have come at the expense of youngster Massa, so he decided against it. But was there any chance he could return in the future? “Formula 1 is constantly changing,” the 37-year-old responded. “The technology, the engines, the rules, the circuits. Once you're out of it, you're out.” Michael Schumacher, Ferrari Michael Schumacher, Ferrari In the end, the attraction of competition proved too strong and Schumacher returned for a three-year stint at Mercedes from 2010 to 2012, during which he struggled to match team-mate Nico Rosberg and scored just one podium finish while topping qualifying on his last Monaco outing. But in the Schumacher camp, one major feeling when he first retired also was relief. When asked by German network RTL what made her happy, his wife, Corinna Schumacher, replied: “That we're all going to go home healthy, that nothing happened in all these years and that we got away with just the one broken leg.” Unfortunately, while the seven-time world champion emerged unscathed from his racing career, he was severely injured in a skiing accident in December 2013. Now 55 years old, he has not been seen in public since then. item.title: Pirates Minor League Awards: Gray Top Player, Hernandez Top Pitcher
item.description: The Pirates spent the week announcing their 2026 minor-league award winners. Murf Gray was named the Honus Wagner Player of the Year and Seth Hernandez was named the Bob Friend Pitcher of the Year. Gray, who also won the Wille Stargell Slugger of the Year, skyrocketed up the system in his first professional season. The 22-year-old began the season with Low-A Bradenton and ended the year in Double-A Altoona. He combined to slash .305/.402/.567 with 27 doubles, 32 home runs and 97 RBI across three levels. Gray, who was drafted by the Pirates in the second round in 2025, led Pittsburgh’s minor league players in hits (143), home runs, RBI, slugging percentage, runs (100), extra-base hits (59) and total bases (266). Hernandez split the year between Bradenton and High-A Greensboro. The ’25 first-round draft pick combined to go 6-1 with a 2.43 ERA in 18 starts. He logged 74 innings, walked 31, struck out 118 and held opponents to a .181 batting average. Hernandez, 20, was placed on the injured list with a season-ending oblique strain on July 25. At the time he landed on the IL, the right-hander was second among all minor-league pitchers in strikeouts. Both Gray (89) and Hernandez (nine) are considered top 100 prospect by MLB Pipeline. Gray is considered the third-best third base prospect. Hernandez is ranked as the top right-hander pitcher. Other Pirates Minor-League Awards Jesus Castillo was named the Bill Mazeroski Defender of the Year. Castillo played every position other than pitcher and catcher in 2026 and committed just nine errors in 288 chances. Yordany De Los Santos won the Omar Moreno Baserunner of the Year after leading the organization with 45 stolen bases in 92 games split between Bradenton and Greensboro. Right-hander Derek Diamond was named the Kent Tekulve Reliever of the Year. Diamond went 7-0 with a 2.45 ERA and a pair of saves in 37 appearances, 29 of which were with Triple-A Indianapolis. Johan De Los Santos was named the Pirates’ rookie level player of the year. The 18-year-old combined to slash .310/.431/.434 with four triples, two home runs, 10 RBI and 26 steals in 31 FCL games before a promotion to Bradenton. Irwin Ramirez was tabbed as the Pirates’ top rookie level pitcher. The right-hander went 1-1 with a 3.67 ERA in eight starts in the Florida Complex League before a promotion to Bradenton. He held opponents to a .157 batting average. The Pirates named Cecilio Beltre as the organization’s staff member of the year. He was a team development coach/mentor for the Dominican Summer League Pirates Gold team. Related Headlines Pirates Top Prospects No. 10: Reinold Navarro and His Ridiculous Strikeout Totals Pirates Top Prospects No. 11: Khristian Curtis Overcomes Adversity to Make MLB Debut Pirates Top Prospects No. 12: Carlos Tejera Starts Fast Read more at Pittsburgh Baseball Now

item.title: Hornell's Mehr named Buffalo Bills Coach of the Week after big win
item.description: The Hornell/Arkport-Canaseraga football program is enjoying a strong 2026 campaign, and the Buffalo Bills have taken notice. Hornell/A-C head coach Dr. Ismail Mehr has been named one of the 2026 High School Tackle Football Coaches of the Week by the Buffalo Bills in partnership with Visa. Mehr was named the Rochester Coach of the Week by the Bills, while the Buffalo Region Coach of the Week was Chad Bartoszek of Salamanca. The weekly honor by the Bills aims to highlight football coaches' efforts on and off the field, recognizing their team's excellence on the field and their service to their communities. As part of the program, each winning coach's program will receive $1,000 from the Buffalo Bills and Visa, and each region's Coach of the Year will receive an additional $1,000 and be celebrated on the field at Highmark Stadium before the Bills vs. Jets game in January. Mehr was honored after leading the Red Raiders to a 19-13 victory over previously undefeated Alexander/Pembroke that moved Hornell/A-C to 6-1 on the season. Tyrone Buchanan sealed the win with a rushing touchdown with under five minutes left in the fourth quarter. Senior running back Matt Karr powered the running game, rushing 12 times for 147 yards and a touchdown. Mehr has been a part of Hornell football for more than two decades, noted the Bills. A 1991 Hornell High School graduate, he returned to his hometown in 2002 after completing medical school and specializing in anesthesiology. He is a board-certified anesthesiologist and medical director at UR Medicine St. James Hospital in Hornell. He began his coaching career as an assistant on the staff of legendary Hornell football coach Gene Mastin . More: Where does Hornell's Mastin now rank after new Section V wins record After years of serving as an assistant coach, Mehr took over as head coach and has led the Red Raiders for the past four seasons. "Community involvement is an important part of the Hornell football program," Mehr told the Bills. "Hornell is a small, blue-collar, hard-working community, and the football program believes strongly in giving back to the community that supports it. As a staff, we encourage our players to be active, responsible, and proud members of the community." This article originally appeared on The Evening Tribune: Hornell's Mehr named Buffalo Bills Coach of the Week after big win

item.title: ESPN analysts believe J.J. McCarthy could lead Giants to playoffs
item.description: New York Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy (18) and New York Giants running back Tyrone Tracy Jr. (29) during a week 6 NFL football game between New York Giants and New Orleans Saints on Sunday, Oct. 18, 2026, at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, NJ. After a season-ending injury to starter Jaxson Dart, the New York Giants have been forced into taking a fluid approach to their starting quarterback situation and are now turning to their third starter of the year. Just over three weeks after trading for J.J. McCarthy, New York is officially moving him to starter and benching Jameis Winston, who relieved Dart. On Thursday’s episode of Get Up, Andrew Hawkins and Adam Schefter discussed what the move could mean not just for the Giants but for the rest of the NFC East as well. “There’s no one who is sticking out in this division, no one who’s playing well,” Hawkins said. “When you look at even the quarterback play throughout the division, I remember when Harbaugh first came, and there was so much excitement around what he could bring to this organization and Jackson Dart and everything he can bring out of him.” “If [J.J. McCarthy] plays the way he did in the 4th [quarter], [the Giants are] the favorites in the division.” @Hawk and @AdamSchefter make bold predictions for the NFC East following the Giants’ change in QB https://t.co/ijvn9Dj7IC — Get Up (@GetUpESPN) October 22, 2026 Hawkins went on to say that McCarthy producing could make the Giants the favorites in the division, which would put New York back in the playoffs. “The conversation was still, well, he’s the fourth-best quarterback in the division. Well, now that we’re this part in the season, no quarterback has really stood out, right? The Giants had their issues and concern, but I would say everything around the quarterback position, obviously, because Jaxson Dart has been out for the New York Giants, has actually looked up a lot quicker than we expected from (tight end Isaiah Likely) of the world. “Nabers looks like a top 10 wide receiver the way we expected before injury. So if you can get a little bit outta J.J., really, they’re in contention. And not only that, they’re probably, for my money, if he plays the way he did in the fourth, the favorites in the division.” Schefter pointed back to how high McCarthy was drafted as a potential indicator of what he’s capable of. “Look, if Jaxson Dart were healthy this year, they would be the favorites to win the division,” he said. “They’re now getting a quarterback who at one point was the 10th overall pick in a draft in where Caleb Williams went one, Jayden Daniels went two, and Drake Maye went three. They believe he’s got that type of ability. If they can harness that type of ability, which the Vikings were willing to just give up on it, and they have a chance to win the division and set up the franchise.” McCarthy’s first start for New York will come on Sunday against the Houston Texans. And not only that, they’re probably, for my money, if he plays the way he did in the fourth, the favorites in the division.” Schefter pointed back to how high McCarthy was drafted as a potential indicator of what he’s capable of. “Look, if Jaxson Dart were healthy this year, they would be the favorites to win the division,” he said. “They’re now getting a quarterback who at one point was the 10th overall pick in a draft in where Caleb Williams went one, Jayden Daniels went two, and Drake Maye went three. They believe he’s got that type of ability. If they can harness that type of ability, which the Vikings were willing to just give up on it, and they have a chance to win the division and set up the franchise.” McCarthy’s first start for New York will come on Sunday against the Houston Texans. item.title: CSD escalates Tebas-Real Madrid dispute with referral to Spanish sports tribunal
item.description: CSD escalates Tebas-Real Madrid dispute with referral to Spanish sports tribunal Spain’s Higher Sports Council (CSD) has referred La Liga president Javier Tebas to the Administrative Tribunal for Sport (TAD) over comments comparing Real Madrid TV’s communication methods to propaganda used by Nazi Germany. The move follows a post published by the La Liga president on X on 16 October, with the CSD asking the independent tribunal to assess whether his remarks could constitute a serious sporting offence. Tebas, who also serves as a vice-president of the Spanish Football Federation (RFEF), made the comparison while criticising Real Madrid’s media approach. The CSD has acted on its own initiative, submitting a reasoned request for the TAD to examine the matter. CSD asks TAD to assess whether Tebas breached Spanish sports law In its statement, the CSD said it had submitted the request because of Tebas’s remarks about Real Madrid. According to the council, the league president compared the club’s communication methods to the “propaganda mechanisms exploited by Goebbels, Minister of Propaganda in Nazi Germany.” CSD statement on Tebas’ comments against Real Madrid. The CSD has asked the TAD to determine whether the comments show evidence of a possible breach of Article 76.4.b of Spain’s Sports Law 10/1990. The provision identifies as serious offences “notorious and public acts that undermine sporting dignity or decorum.” The referral does not establish that Tebas has committed an offence. Instead, it asks the TAD, an independent collegiate body, to assess whether the remarks fall within the scope of the legislation. CSD highlights the importance of respect in Spanish sport The council’s submission also refers to the TAD’s own legal doctrine, based on Supreme Court jurisprudence, concerning the meaning of sporting dignity and decorum. According to the CSD, these principles are linked to maintaining a civilised environment in sport, which requires mutual respect between people holding significant positions within the sporting community. The council also stressed the importance of protecting the values that allow sport to function as a space for respect, coexistence and fair play. Tebas in hot waters after controversial statements. (Photo by Jan Kruger/Getty Images for Soccerex) Tebas’s position as La Liga president and the RFEF vice-president places him among Spanish football’s most prominent administrators, making the dispute particularly significant given the institutional relationships between the league, the RFEF and Real Madrid. The CSD’s intervention moves the controversy beyond a public dispute between Tebas and Real Madrid. The TAD must now assess whether the comments meet the legal threshold for a serious sporting offence, rather than simply determine whether they were inflammatory. According to Calciomercato.com , the Brazilian defender has reportedly attracted interest from Bayer Leverkusen , who are ready to explore a move to bring him to Germany during the winter transfer window. The centre-back, born in 1997, recently sparked controversy with comments about some teammates’ lack of character following the defeat to Lazio, an issue that was subsequently resolved with an apology to Luciano Spalletti . Juventus do not consider Bremer untouchable, but his departure would depend on a particularly high offer. The defender is a key member of the squad, earning around €6 million per season . Any move therefore hinges on Bayer’s willingness to meet Juventus’ financial demands, as the club have no intention of easily letting go of one of their most important players. 🤩 Milan dream of Scott, with two more midfield targets Milan are exploring potential moves to strengthen their midfield, assessing targets for January or next summer. However, Milan will not be able to use today’s match to watch the player, born in 2003, up close, as he is injured. Top of the list is Alex Scott , the Bournemouth midfielder who has impressed in the Premier League and is also being tracked by several leading English clubs. However, Milan will not be able to use today’s match to watch the player, born in 2003, up close, as he is injured. A deal would be difficult regardless, with the Cherries hoping to sell their star for a fee close to €100 million. According to TMW , the other two targets would be easier to land: Yasin Ayari of Brighton and Adem Zorgane of Union Saint-Gilloise. The former can play both as a holding midfielder and an attacking midfielder, and his contract expires in 2027, a detail that could influence the English club’s valuation. Milan are monitoring the various situations without having settled on a definitive strategy: opportunities over the coming months will determine which targets they pursue. ✍️ Inter begin talks over Thuram contract extension Inter are stepping up efforts to secure Marcus Thuram ’s long-term future. The French striker’s contract expires in 2028, but both sides want to begin talks now over an extension. According to TMW , initial contacts have been positive, paving the way for formal negotiations. The aim is to agree a deal running until 2030 , strengthening the bond between Inter and one of their key attacking players. Talks will continue over the coming weeks, with both sides keen to reach an agreement quickly. Their shared desire to continue together is an important first step towards a new deal. 🙅‍♂️ Napoli, ADL: "I’m not selling! I turned down €3.5 billion" Aurelio De Laurentiis has dismissed rumours of a possible sale of Napoli to American businessman Matt Rizzetta . Speaking to Radio Kiss Kiss , the Napoli president ruled out any intention of selling the club: " Napoli is not for sale. I have no intention of proceeding ." De Laurentiis also explained that, if he ever decided to sell, he would prefer to hand the club over to a Neapolitan businessman rather than an American. The owner also reiterated his determination to press ahead with plans to build a new stadium, stressing that he had already rejected huge offers in the past. " Years ago, I turned down €3.5 billion from Arab buyers ," he said. As for Rizzetta, De Laurentiis confirmed that he had received an approach about a potential sale, but had replied that there was no intention of selling Napoli. 🔜 Roma: Bakola a target, but not for January Roma are keeping a close eye on Bakola , Sassuolo’s young French midfielder, who has also attracted interest from Juventus and several Premier League clubs. According to TMW , however, Sassuolo have no intention of letting him go during the winter transfer window. Having arrived from Marseille last February for close to €10 million, the French youngster has already made eight appearances across Serie A and the Coppa Italia, catching the eye of several clubs with his ability. Sassuolo see Bakola as an important player for the second half of the season and aim to keep him until at least June as they look to secure comfortable survival under Alberto Aquilani . A January move therefore looks difficult for Roma: Sassuolo’s management appear unwilling to enter negotiations during this transfer window and would prefer to postpone any decisions on the midfielder’s future until the summer. 🤕 Lazio, Gud’s return delayed! Albert Gudmundsson will have to wait a little longer before returning to action. According to Il Messaggero , the latest examinations showed that the bone callus in his right shoulder has not yet fully formed. The forward will therefore miss the first matches of November and is targeting a return after the international break. Ahead of the match against Parma, Marusic and Rovella remain unavailable, while Cancellieri is ready to return to the squad. Cataldi is also nearing a return and could rotate with Belahyane to manage workloads in midfield. 😔 Fiorentina, Antognoni regrets missing centenary celebrations Giancarlo Antognoni has reflected on his decision not to attend Fiorentina ’s centenary celebrations, organised by the Commisso family. " I do feel some regret about not going, for the fans, not for the owners ," he told Torpedone , the Autolinee Toscane podcast, explaining that past disagreements had influenced his decision. The former Fiorentina icon nevertheless stressed that he had never had any problems with Joseph Commisso or Rocco’s wife, Catherine. Antognoni also commented on the team’s current situation, calling for the squad to be given time following a turnover of 13 players. " You can’t have everything straight away with such sweeping changes," he stressed, expressing confidence in Paolo Vanoli ’s work. This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. item.title: Alex Pereira drops heartbreaking UFC retirement update
item.description: Alex Pereira drops heartbreaking UFC retirement update appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Striving for a win, UFC star Alex Pereira might now be considering hanging up his gloves and announcing his retirement. Pereira, 39, a former UFC light heavyweight and middleweight champion, still has goals left to achieve. However, the veteran plans to retire once the results start going against him. After losing to Ciryl Gane in their Heavyweight championship fight at UFC Freedom 250 at the White House, the Brazilian is looking to make his way back by becoming the UFC’s first-ever triple champion. Pereira has lost two of his last three fights. He is next scheduled to fight Sergei Pavlovich at UFC 335. A victory there could open his path to a showdown with the winner of Ciryl Gane’s title defense against Josh Hokit. However, recently, speaking on The Ariel Helwani Show, Pereira dropped an unfortunate update about his career’s future. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “You gotta learn how to see when it’s your moment and when it’s not,” Pereira said. “If one day I start losing, if things start not going too good, I don’t want to be a stepping stone for nobody to be going up. I’ll just be focusing on enjoying my time and enjoying my money. “We did a very good career plan for me, my kids, my future, my kids’ future, for the institute that I built,” he added. “We’re all settled, so I have nothing to prove anymore.” Once regarded as one of the greatest fighters under multiple weight divisions, his recent array of losses could be an indication toward him finishing his career. Related: Veteran MMA fighter gives update on Conor McGregor’s injury comeback Related: Conor McGregor addresses his UFC success reasons

item.title: Bernardo Silva: “I am very happy to have scored my first goal with this jersey”
item.description: Real Madrid midfielder Bernardo Silva scored the team’s opening goal against Red Bull Leipzig, his first goal as a madridista, and talked to the club’s media after the game. “I am very happy to have won this game and scored my first goal with this jersey. It was a tough match, where I think we were much better in the second half than in the first. In the first half, we created some chances but also allowed them to approach our goal quite a bit. Thibaut was very important for us. In the second half, we controlled the game much better, and in the end, we secured a good victory. We are happy and will keep moving forward,” he said. Bernardo also explained what Mourinho wants from the midfielders. “It doesn’t matter who is on the pitch. We are a team with very aggressive and strong players in one-on-one situations, who love dribbling and making runs into space. We need to find the balance between maintaining possession, finding the forwards, and being direct. We want to play fluid football, and we are getting to know each other better and trying to improve. I think the team has improved a lot in recent games, and I’m sure it will continue to do so soon. We need to strike that balance between controlling possession and the game while also not being a boring team, staying intense and aggressive, as Real Madrid has always been. That’s difficult, and you need to be very prepared to do it well,” he added. He also talked about his role. “I keep working. I’m ready to help this club. Whether it’s one minute, five, ten, or ninety… I’ll be training well, helping the group, and the day the coach feels he needs me, I’ll be ready,” he explained.

item.title: Three Numbers Define The Braves’ Offseason Choices
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Atlanta Braves stand at a crossroads this winter. The team needs to decide how to keep their ace on the mound and fix a broken lineup. Three specific numbers from the 2026 season show exactly where the pressure lies. These figures are the map for the front office. The Ace and the Rotation Depth Chris Sale posted a 196 Adjusted ERA+ in his third year with Atlanta. According to MLB.com , only Greg Maddux and Reynaldo López have ever posted a better mark for the Braves in a season with at least 25 starts. Sale threw his four-seamer at 96.1 mph on average. This was the highest velocity of his career. He did not miss a single day due to injury. The key to his success was rest. The team gave him extra days off between starts. This worked perfectly for a pitcher in his age-37 season. But the rotation behind him is shaky. According to MLB.com, the sole current members forecasted to log at least 25 starts in the coming season are Sale, Grant Holmes, and Bryce Elder. Reynaldo López has a right shoulder issue that will likely limit him. Spencer Schwellenbach faces great uncertainty with a screw in his right elbow. The Braves have young talent like Spencer Strider and AJ Smith-Shawver. But they also have questions about their health and role. If Schwellenbach and Strider are healthy, should they start or pitch out of the bullpen? The team might need to add two starters this winter to keep Sale fresh. Re-signing Tyler Mahle would be a big win. Without him, the depth could run thin. The Shortstop Hole and the Dubón Decision The offense was a major problem in 2024. The Braves received a 67 Weighted Runs Created Plus from the shortstop position. This means the production at that spot was 33 percent below league average. The team also struggled at third base, left field, and second base. But the shortstop gap is the most glaring. It might be the easiest to fix. Mauricio Dubón proved he can handle the position. When playing shortstop, Dubón produced a 115 wRC+. He also had a Fielding Run Value of +3. He showed he could be an everyday player. The question is whether to make him the starter or keep him as a versatile utility man. One year ago, the Braves landed him because the Astros did not want to pay him approximately $6 million. Keeping Dubón as the everyday shortstop makes sense. If the team moves him to other spots, they leave a huge hole at shortstop. The Braves must decide if his versatility is more valuable than his bat at shortstop. The answer seems clear based on the 115 wRC+ he posted there. Looking at the Farm System While the big league team faces tough choices, the farm system is getting better. The Braves have young stars ready to help. Eric Hartman, the team’s No. 1 prospect, hit 24 homers and stole 38 bases in 94 games for High-A Rome. He entered the year as the No. 20 prospect and finished as a Top 40 prospect. But he hit just .182 with a .577 OPS after a promotion to Double-A. He must improve against better pi

item.title: 3 Players Heat Traded Lead Bucks in Scoring in Opener
item.description: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - OCTOBER 16: Tyler Herro #11of the Milwaukee Bucks dribbles the ball against the Indiana Pacers at Gainbridge Fieldhouse on October 16, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) Getty The Milwaukee Bucks started a new era on Wednesday night — the post-Giannis Antetokounmpo period of the franchise. It’s a painful reality to face, that the best player to ever don a Bucks uniform is gone, traded to the Miami Heat. All the Bucks can do is move forward, and they didn’t get off to a great start of that with a 128-116 loss to the Washington Wizards to open their season on Wednesday. There were positive signs, though, mostly coming from the players they got in return for Giannis. In fact, three of the trade return players were the three-leading scorers for the Bucks on Wednesday. And for what it’s worth, the Heat lost their opener to, falling to the Minnesota Timberwolves . So improvements can be made all around. Tyler Herro Debut Tyler Herro is a Milwaukee-native, so it’s got to be special for him to get to play for the Bucks. Wednesday’s game was on the road, not yet home cooking for Herro, but he did lead Milwaukee in scoring. Herro put up 24 points on 9-for-21 from the floor, including 4-for-11 from 3, while making both his attempted foul shots. Herro added nine assists, two rebounds and a steal while turning the ball over four times. He’s going to have to lead the Bucks in scoring most nights to have a chance. Jaime Jaquez The forward Jaime Jaquez had a great Bucks debut after coming over in the Giannis trade. He put up 22 points on 8-for-12 from the field, including 1-for-3 from 3, and made 5-of-6 free throws. Jaquez also had seven rebounds and two assists while turning it over twice. He was the only member of the Bucks without a negative plus-minus (his was actually 0). Kasparas Jakucionis Jakucionis was just drafted in 2025, but he had a great start for the Bucks after the trade. He put up 15 points on 4-for-7 shooting, including 1-for-3 from 3, while making all six of his foul shots. Jakucionis added three rebounds and three assists with one block and one turnover. Kel’el Ware Ware was the quietest player to have arrived in the Giannis trade. He got 14 minutes off the bench and put up seven points with three rebounds, one assist, one steal and one turnover. Ware was 3-for-6 from the floor, but 0-for-2 from 3 and 1-for-3 from the foul line. It could be tough for Ware to play much more in the early going with Jaquez, Kyle Kuzma and Myles Turner all in the starting lineup, and on Wednesday, Ousmane Dieng got more minutes off the bench, too. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post 3 Players Heat Traded Lead Bucks in Scoring in Opener appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: How much money does Gianni Infantino make at FIFA? FIFA responds to retracted report over compensation
item.description: How much money does Gianni Infantino make at FIFA? FIFA responds to retracted report over compensation originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Editor's note: this story was originally published on October 13 with information from a report by The Times which has since been retracted, as reflected in the update on October 21. Ever since the conclusion of the 2026 FIFA World Cup this past summer, the heat has been on Gianni Infantino's position as FIFA president. The whirlwind began when Infantino had proposed selling shares of the World Cup to private equity investors, which sent fans and fellow executives into a frenzy. This scandal resulted in Infantino's position being called into question, and created a tense atmosphere in the lead-up to the upcoming FIFA presidential elections to come next spring. Now, Infantino has once again been placed in the spotlight after a report — which has since been retracted — claimed he was being paid extra compensation in addition to what FIFA disclosed publicly in its 2025 annual report. However, that report has since been retracted, sparking a heavy response from FIFA. MORE: Ranking the top candidates for the 2026 Ballon d'Or Gianni Infantino salary as FIFA president FIFA has committed to publishing president Gianni Infantino's salary each year in its annual report, declaring his compensation in the company's yearly release. For the 2025 calendar year, Infantino was paid 4.8 million Swiss Francs (CHF), or $5.76 million in gross salary, according to FIFA's annual compensation report . This is broken down into 2.6 million CHF in base salary, and 2.2 million CHF in bonuses. Report about undisclosed payment to FIFA president is retracted According to a report by Martyn Ziegler of The Times , which has since been publicly retracted, Gianni Infantino was paid additionally on top of his disclosed salary by FIFA. The report cites 2024 U.S. tax filings by FIFA which show that Infantino was given $1.76 million by FWC2026, the company FIFA set up to run the 2026 FIFA World Cup in the United States this past summer. U.S.-based non-profits must fill out IRS form 990, on which FIFA disclosed to the U.S. government payments by FWC2026 to Infantino as well as FIFA General Secretary Matias Graffstrom, CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani, and a number of other executives involved in the tournament's production. This payment came on top of his regularly reported compensation, and was not publicly disclosed in FIFA's financial filings in their annual report. However, this report was officially retracted on October 20 by The Times who conceded that FIFA's report did not disclose this additional income because Swiss tax law rules do not count expense and reimbursement payments as compensation with regards to filings and reportings by non-profits. item.content:encoded: How much money does Gianni Infantino make at FIFA? FIFA responds to retracted report over compensation originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Editor's note: this story was originally published on October 13 with information from a report by The Times which has since been retracted, as reflected in the update on October 21. Ever since the conclusion of the 2026 FIFA World Cup this past summer, the heat has been on Gianni Infantino's position as FIFA president. The whirlwind began when Infantino had proposed selling shares of the World Cup to private equity investors, which sent fans and fellow executives into a frenzy. This scandal resulted in Infantino's position being called into question, and created a tense atmosphere in the lead-up to the upcoming FIFA presidential elections to come next spring. Now, Infantino has once again been placed in the spotlight after a report — which has since been retracted — claimed he was being paid extra compensation in addition to what FIFA disclosed publicly in its 2025 annual report. However, that report has since been retracted, sparking a heavy response from FIFA. MORE: Ranking the top candidates for the 2026 Ballon d'Or Gianni Infantino salary as FIFA president FIFA has committed to publishing president Gianni Infantino's salary each year in its annual report, declaring his compensation in the company's yearly release. For the 2025 calendar year, Infantino was paid 4.8 million Swiss Francs (CHF), or $5.76 million in gross salary, according to FIFA's annual compensation report . This is broken down into 2.6 million CHF in base salary, and 2.2 million CHF in bonuses. Report about undisclosed payment to FIFA president is retracted According to a report by Martyn Ziegler of The Times , which has since been publicly retracted, Gianni Infantino was paid additionally on top of his disclosed salary by FIFA. The report cites 2024 U.S. tax filings by FIFA which show that Infantino was given $1.76 million by FWC2026, the company FIFA set up to run the 2026 FIFA World Cup in the United States this past summer. U.S.-based non-profits must fill out IRS form 990, on which FIFA disclosed to the U.S. government payments by FWC2026 to Infantino as well as FIFA General Secretary Matias Graffstrom, CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani, and a number of other executives involved in the tournament's production. This payment came on top of his regularly reported compensation, and was not publicly disclosed in FIFA's financial filings in their annual report. However, this report was officially retracted on October 20 by The Times who conceded that FIFA's report did not disclose this additional income because Swiss tax law rules do not count expense and reimbursement payments as compensation with regards to filings and reportings by non-profits. They also acknowledged that claims regarding a Miami property purchase were false. FIFA assert that Infantino's payments from FWC2026 were not part of his regular salary or compensation, and therefore were not required to be disclosed in their annual report by Swiss tax law, and therefore, while included in the U.S. tax filings, were not required to be publicly announced. FIFA & FIFA PRESIDENT RECEIVES APOLOGY FROM ‘THE TIMES’ FIFA takes note of an apology published today by The Times following an inaccurate and damaging report: On 13 October 2026 (Sport), we reported that Gianni Infantino received a "second salary" from Fifa, which Fifa had failed to disclose. This is incorrect. There was no “second salary.” Regulations do not require Fifa to include expenses and reimbursements received by Mr Infantino in its annual report as they are not considered "compensation" under Swiss reporting requirements. We also accept Mr Infantino did not purchase a property in Miami at a suspected undervalue as we reported and neither he nor his family are the legal or beneficial owners of Shadi LLC and have no control over that company, as we suggested. We are happy to make these corrections and apologise to Mr Infantino and Fifa for the errors. As FIFA stated in August, it is evident that there is a concerted and ongoing effort by some to undermine FIFA and its President. FIFA urges the media to act responsibly and carefully verify all sourcing to prevent the publication and subsequent reproduction of false and defamatory information. FIFA welcomes legitimate scrutiny. But scrutiny is not a license to amplify false allegations. Where reporting is inaccurate, misleading, or totally false, as in this case, FIFA will continue to challenge it directly and vigorously. — FIFA Media (@fifamedia) October 20, 2026 Following the retraction, FIFA acknowledged the apology they received from The Times and warned there was a "concerted and ongoing effort by some to undermine FIFA and its President."

item.title: Patriots’ Mike Vrabel Issues Warning About Bears’ Ben Johnson Before TNF
item.description: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - OCTOBER 04: Head coach Mike Vrabel of the New England Patriots reacts after a play against the Buffalo Bills during the second quarter at Highmark Stadium on October 04, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Bryan M. Bennett/Getty Images) Getty CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 04: Head coach Ben Johnson of the Chicago Bears reacts during the second quarter of the game against the New York Jets at Soldier Field on October 04, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Jessie Alcheh/Getty Images) Getty ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 18: Caleb Williams #18 and Kalif Raymond #14 of the Chicago Bears celebrate a touchdown against the Atlanta Falcons during the first quarter of the game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) Getty The New England Patriots have much to ponder ahead of Thursday night’s matchup against the Chicago Bears. And head coach Mike Vrabel knows that preparing for Ben Johnson’s offense is rarely clear-cut. The Bears coach has a reputation for keeping defenses guessing with atypical formations, plus aggressive fourth-down decisions and a trick play thrown in. Vrabel is wary of that unpredictability marching into Soldier Field. Vrabel Points to Johnson’s Unpredictable Play-Calling Getty CHICAGO, ILLINOIS – OCTOBER 04: Head coach Ben Johnson of the Chicago Bears reacts during the second quarter of the game against the New York Jets at Soldier Field on October 04, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Jessie Alcheh/Getty Images) Asked about the biggest challenge of preparing for Johnson, Vrabel pointed to the sheer number of possibilities Chicago puts out there. “There’s a lot of volume. They do a lot of things well, and you’ll have to be prepared for some unscouted looks,” Vrabel said during his October 21 press conference . “But he stays aggressive. He has a lot of faith in those guys on fourth down. He marries up formations and motions.” Seeing something unexpected from Johnson can happen even with limited preparation time. When asked whether the Bears HC might unveil an unscouted look on a Thursday night, Vrabel remembered an example. “They handed the ball to the left tackle, who was going to throw a pass on four days in Detroit, so probably,” he said. Vrabel was referencing a trick play involving Penei Sewell during the Detroit Lions ‘ Thanksgiving matchup against Chicago in November 2024. Sewell took a reverse and prepared to throw the football before taking a sack when nobody was open. The play lost yardage, but it illustrated Johnson’s willingness to put the ball in unanticipated hands. The former Lions offensive coordinator has that creativity in (and before) his second season leading Chicago. Against the Atlanta Falcons on October 18, Johnson’s offense successfully executed a hook-and-ladder involving Caleb Williams , Rome Odunze and Roschon Johnson . The play gained 12 yards and moved the chains. Patriots Go to War With Bears’ Offense Getty ATLANTA

(Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) The trick plays are only part of what Vrabel’s defense will need to meet with tact. Chicago has also demonstrated an ability to sustain possessions and control the tempo of games. According to Patriots.com’s Evan Lazar , the Bears are averaging 73.2 offensive plays per game while their opponents are running just 50.2. That disparity has allowed Johnson’s offense to dictate the pace, while making it tougher for opposing quarterbacks to get the ball in their hands. Chicago also leads the NFL with 15 fourth-down attempts, reflecting the aggressive approach Vrabel highlighted. Since this Patriots team is bogged down by injuries throughout its roster, notably along the offensive line, those longer possessions pose an obstacle. Vrabel stressed turning the tables. “That’s the challenge, is being able to flip the script a little bit, not let them run 73 plays and only have to defend 50,” he said. New England enters the contest with a 4-2 record, matching Chicago’s mark through six games. item.title: Rangers Daily: Sully pushes back; Crazy Ottawa return for Brady Tkachuk
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Mike Sullivan apparently heard the outside noise and wanted to set the record straight about certain poor underlying metrics for the New York Rangers defensemen so far this season. As reported in several spaces, including here in a recent article published by Tom Castro , the Rangers spend a lot of time defending, are being out-chanced, and have a mediocre expected goal share — collectively as a team, and individually by player. Castro pointed these things out, backed up by underlying metrics from Natural Stat Trick , and stated that it’s something the Rangers should have some level of concern about. Of course, the Rangers are 7-3-1 to start the season and certainly pass the eye test in most areas of their play. Their defensive zone exits are much crisper and cleaner, and the support and structure sure appear better than in previous seasons. A big part of that is that New York works much better now in five-man groups with the forwards much more dedicated to playing a 200-foot game, which Castro rightly pointed out. But Sullivan also correctly argued that one can’t simply look at any one stat or underlying metric in a vacuum to form a complete opinion. “When you start looking at metrics and things of that nature, context is really important. If you don’t understand context, it’s hard for you to interpret data the right way,” the Rangers coach said Wednesday . “So for example, if there’s a defense pair or a line combination that gets a lot of defensive-zone starts against the other team’s top players, they’re probably going to be on the ice for some chances against. But they might limit the quality of the chance or the quantity of the chances of the other team’s top players, and they keep them off the board, and we have success because of it. Their metrics might not look positive, but the value is they help us win.” Specifically speaking about the team’s new second defense pairing of Marcus Pettersson and Sean Durzi , there’s no question the Rangers are much better off with those two veterans in that role than any combinations they put together in recent years. I pointed to that is the Rangers Daily column on Wednesday. “When you look at multiple data points, it gives you a little bit of a better picture of what that context is or what it looks like. So, we believe Marcus and ‘Durz’ have given us pretty good minutes,” Sullivan explained. “Some nights they’ve been better than others, without a doubt. But I also think there’s more to it than (the analytics).” Fair enough. Analytics are important. So, too, are results, the eye test, the human element. That’s why the Yankees bringing back the analytics-driven Aaron Boone as manager draws so much criticism from fans and reporters alike, because it’s so one-sided how he runs that team and goes about making his decisions. Sully appears to have a good balance of both in how he oversees the Rangers. New York Rangers news and analysis Brad Penner-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IM

New York Rangers news and analysis Brad Penner-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect With stick taps to longtime AHL beat reporter Patrick Williams, we take a dive into explaining Dylan Garand’s success with the Rangers , focusing more on what’s between his ears than the technical aspects. Tomas Chrenko heating up in Slovakia tops Steven Voogel’s report on Rangers prospects playing in Europe. This is pretty cool: in the most recent NCAA men’s hockey rankings, the top five teams each has one Rangers prospect playing on it , including No. 1- ranked Michigan, with forward Malcolm Spence . Keith Yandle shared a story on a recent podcast about why he opted to reject a contract offer to remain with the Rangers back in the summer of 2016. NHL news and rumors Marc DesRosiers-Imagn Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect TSN : It was quite the theater in Ottawa on Wednesday night, when Senators fan brought their A Game and directed a heaping dose of vitriol at former captain Brady Tkachuk in his return after forcing a trade to the Florida Panthers this past offseason. Oh, and the Senators won 5-1, despite Brady scoring the first goal of the contest. Sportsnet : Nice job by the Sportsnet crew putting together this highlight video showcasing the creative chants from the Senators fans directed at Brady Tkachuk in his return to Canadian Tire Cnetre. Florida Hockey Now : George Richards has this take from the Panthers side of an eventful night in Ottawa. TSN : Some potentially bad news in an otherwise excellent night for the Senators: No. 1 goalie Linus Ullmark left the game in the third period with a lower-body injury. New Jersey Hockey Now : James Nichols takes a deep dive into what it would take for the Devils to trade for Dylan Larkin and fit him under their salary cap. Pittsburgh Hockey Now: Penguins coach Dan Muse said in a radio interview that forward Ben Kindel is doing better and could return to Pittsburgh by time you read this following a medical episode that forced the team charter to return to Salt Lake City so that he could be rushed to a local hospital there. Sportsnet : Some really good news for the defending Stanley Cup champs as talented forward Seth Jarvis will make his season debut for the Carolina Hurricanes against the Edmonton Oilers on Thursday following offseason shoulder surgery. item.title: Xbox Officially Confirms Cloud Gaming’s New Pay-As-You-Go Prices
item.description: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma continues to make significant changes as part of a major reset to rebuild the brand. Nearly 2,000 employees have been let go, and three more rounds of layoffs are expected between October and January. In addition to mass layoffs, gaming services are also being affected, with Xbox Cloud Gaming adding a pay-as-you-go policy. Paid Xbox Cloud Gaming services will begin in November, and prices have now been revealed.

item.title: 2027: PRP alleges multi-million naira plot to break its ranks, sabotage opposition coalition
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The Peoples Redemption Party (PRP) has alleged a plot by senior members of the ruling party to destabilise its ranks, sabotage its grassroots structures and undermine efforts to build a credible opposition coalition ahead of the 2027 general elections. The party said the alleged scheme involved hundreds of millions of naira to compromise its officials, exploit former members and create divisions capable of weakening its electoral fortunes. In a statement by its National Chairman, Dr. Hakeem Baba-Ahmed, the PRP alerted its members and the public to the alleged plot, warning supporters against inducements to work against the party. It alleged that some disgraced former members were being deployed to create the impression of internal division, while strategically placed party officers were being used to undermine its grassroots support. The PRP specifically warned against attempts by unauthorised persons to recruit polling agents in its name, urging members to resist and expose any financial inducements intended to divert their support. “The persons in the governing party involved in this scheme have been advised to steer clear of the PRP and distance themselves from attempts to create a fictional PRP with their party’s funds and their names,” the statement said. The party warned that serving officers found to be involved would face disciplinary action, insisting that neither financial inducements nor internal sabotage would make it abandon its political commitments. “The leadership of the PRP wishes to assure its candidates and Party supporters that it will not sacrifice their commitments and loyalty at any price,” Baba-Ahmed said. The PRP said it remained committed to challenging the continuation of the Tinubu administration beyond 2027 and playing a role in building a potentially winning opposition coalition. The post 2027: PRP alleges multi-million naira plot to break its ranks, sabotage opposition coalition appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Terrorism: Court jails man 40 years for spying for late Benue militia leader
item.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri, Abuja The Federal High Court in Abuja on Thursday convicted and sentenced a man, Sunday Frank, to 40 years in prison after he confessed that he served as a spy for an alleged notorious bandit leader in Benue State, Terwase Akwaza, popularly known as Gana. Gana, who reportedly began as part of a militia group defending Benue communities against attacks by suspected herdsmen, was killed in September 2020 by security operatives. In a four-count charge brought before the court by the federal government, it alleged that the convict, Frank, who hails from Katsina-Ala Local Government Area of Benue State, monitored and provided information to Gana about the movement of security agents. It alleged that the convict’s coverage for Gana spanned Benue and Taraba states. Specifically, in the charge, which was personally prosecuted by the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Prince Lateef Fagbemi, SAN, it was alleged that the convict had also kidnapped one Samuel in 2022 and held him hostage until the sum of N40,000 was paid for his release. He was accused of committing offences contrary to sections 21 and 24 of the Terrorism Prevention and Prohibition Act (TPPA) 2022. Even though the defendant denied counts 1, 2 and 3 of the charge, which related to his alleged involvement in abduction, he pleaded guilty to count 4, which related to providing information to the Benue bandit leader. Following his plea, the AGF applied for the counts the defendant denied to be struck out, a request the court granted. Afterwards, the prosecution produced a witness who told the court that he was part of the team that investigated the defendant. He mounted the witness box and reviewed the facts of the case. The witness, simply identified as “AAA” after the court gave the FG permission to shield his real name, said the defendant had confessed to being a bandit and an informant to the late Gana. He said the defendant, who was arrested in 2022, admitted that aside from giving updates on the movement of security agents to Gana, he also confessed to his involvement in banditry and participation in the abduction of two persons. According to the witness, the defendant’s confessions were both oral and written. The FG’s application to tender the statement in evidence was not opposed by the defence lawyer, Mr Y. Y. Shullai. Consequently, trial judge Hawa Yilwa admitted and marked the defendant’s statement as Exhibit A. The witness further told the court that his team investigated the defendant’s activities and filed a report. The report was tendered and admitted as Exhibit B. In his submissions, the AGF stressed that, in view of the defendant’s confession and the exhibits, he should be convicted on count 4 of the charge, to which he pleaded guilty. item.dc:creator: Ayobami
item.content:encoded: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri, Abuja The Federal High Court in Abuja on Thursday convicted and sentenced a man, Sunday Frank, to 40 years in prison after he confessed that he served as a spy for an alleged notorious bandit leader in Benue State, Terwase Akwaza, popularly known as Gana. Gana, who reportedly began as part of a militia group defending Benue communities against attacks by suspected herdsmen, was killed in September 2020 by security operatives. In a four-count charge brought before the court by the federal government, it alleged that the convict, Frank, who hails from Katsina-Ala Local Government Area of Benue State, monitored and provided information to Gana about the movement of security agents. It alleged that the convict’s coverage for Gana spanned Benue and Taraba states. Specifically, in the charge, which was personally prosecuted by the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Prince Lateef Fagbemi, SAN, it was alleged that the convict had also kidnapped one Samuel in 2022 and held him hostage until the sum of N40,000 was paid for his release. He was accused of committing offences contrary to sections 21 and 24 of the Terrorism Prevention and Prohibition Act (TPPA) 2022. Even though the defendant denied counts 1, 2 and 3 of the charge, which related to his alleged involvement in abduction, he pleaded guilty to count 4, which related to providing information to the Benue bandit leader. Following his plea, the AGF applied for the counts the defendant denied to be struck out, a request the court granted. Afterwards, the prosecution produced a witness who told the court that he was part of the team that investigated the defendant. He mounted the witness box and reviewed the facts of the case. The witness, simply identified as “AAA” after the court gave the FG permission to shield his real name, said the defendant had confessed to being a bandit and an informant to the late Gana. He said the defendant, who was arrested in 2022, admitted that aside from giving updates on the movement of security agents to Gana, he also confessed to his involvement in banditry and participation in the abduction of two persons. According to the witness, the defendant’s confessions were both oral and written. The FG’s application to tender the statement in evidence was not opposed by the defence lawyer, Mr Y. Y. Shullai. Consequently, trial judge Hawa Yilwa admitted and marked the defendant’s statement as Exhibit A. The witness further told the court that his team investigated the defendant’s activities and filed a report. The report was tendered and admitted as Exhibit B. In his submissions, the AGF stressed that, in view of the defendant’s confession and the exhibits, he should be convicted on count 4 of the charge, to which he pleaded guilty. The AGF described the offence as very serious, noting that the law prescribes a punishment of at least 20 years’ imprisonment and a maximum of life imprisonment. “I urge my lord to hand down a sentence of not less than 30 years. This is a very serious offence. “If it is not nipped in the bud, a whole generation of our security operatives can be wiped out by people like this providing information about their movement,” the AGF added. He further drew the court’s attention to the fact that count 4 of the charge related to section 13 of the TPPA. The defence counsel, who is from the Legal Aid Council of Nigeria (LACoN), said he was not opposed to the AGF’s submissions. Therefore, Justice Yilwa found the defendant guilty and sentenced him to 40 years in prison, starting from the day of his arrest. The court held that the convict should, upon completing his prison term, be subjected to a rehabilitation and deradicalisation programme. The case is part of the ongoing mass trial of detained terror suspects. The post Terrorism: Court jails man 40 years for spying for late Benue militia leader appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Forget "Malaise 2.0," GM says it's still all-in on EVs and autonomy
item.description: GM provided flights from Detroit to New York and accommodation so Ars could attend the GM Future event. Ars does not accept paid editorial content. It’s easy to criticize US automakers and their tepid approach to electric vehicles under the current administration and the expiration of the EV tax credit . It’s also easy to look at the rest of the world's embrace of EVs and wonder if the US is entering a “Malaise 2.0” era. Which is why GM wants the world to know that it is still focused on its end goals of electrification, autonomy, and improving vehicle quality while reducing development time. At this year’s GM Forward event, company executives announced that its hands-off, eyes-off Super Cruise technology will expand across the lineup and be available on nearly every vehicle. This will include the pickup trucks and the crossovers, and not just the Escalade IQ that it was announced for last year. Sterling Anderson, GM’s head of product, said the company is testing this technology to the tune of 1 million miles (1.6 million km) a month in both the virtual and real world. The goal is that not only would the vehicle be able to take you places, but it could go and do things for you. Read full article Comments

item.title: Nvidia's Huang: Don't mention the AI-pocalypse
item.description: Jensen Huang wants the world to stop fretting about AI and start building with it. At Nvidia's GTC event in Berlin, he dismissed predictions of human extinction, defended AI's job prospects, and pitched a $4,000 computer as the family robot. The Nvidia chief's relentless optimism occasionally gave way to irritation during a question-and-answer session. "If we don't describe a future worthy to be part of, then we're not going to lead people there," he said. "We have to describe a future worthy of creating. We have to describe a future not of fear, but of optimism. Who wants to create a future that's worse than today's? We don't have to work hard to create a future worse than today. We just let it happen, isn't that right?" Huang said that we still have to ask the hard questions about safety and jobs, but "it's important, of course, that we don't make it up. It is not helpful in describing an optimistic future when you say that it will be the end of the human civilization. First of all, it's not true. It's made up. I know it gets headlines," he said, dismissing such stories as clickbait. We're exploring the universe of design options that are within the constraints that we care about, that are physical or realistic constraints." item.dc:creator: Dan Robinson
item.content:encoded: Jensen Huang wants the world to stop fretting about AI and start building with it. At Nvidia's GTC event in Berlin, he dismissed predictions of human extinction, defended AI's job prospects, and pitched a $4,000 computer as the family robot. The Nvidia chief's relentless optimism occasionally gave way to irritation during a question-and-answer session. "If we don't describe a future worthy to be part of, then we're not going to lead people there," he said. "We have to describe a future worthy of creating. We have to describe a future not of fear, but of optimism. Who wants to create a future that's worse than today's? We don't have to work hard to create a future worse than today. We just let it happen, isn't that right?" Huang said that we still have to ask the hard questions about safety and jobs, but "it's important, of course, that we don't make it up. It is not helpful in describing an optimistic future when you say that it will be the end of the human civilization. First of all, it's not true. It's made up. I know it gets headlines," he said, dismissing such stories as clickbait. When asked if AI really makes people more productive, he explained that there are two ways to think about that: either it helps you do the same old thing more efficiently, or it helps you do things you couldn't before. "Most of engineering, most of design, has to do with exploring options. Try, experiment, try and experiment, iterate, experiment, iterate," he said. "What's the best combination? And you can only have so much time to try different versions. Now I have AI to go off and explore that universe. That is productivity. And inside our company, we do this every single day now. We're exploring the universe of design options that are within the constraints that we care about, that are physical or realistic constraints." Huang pointed to construction and infrastructure work generated by the AI datacenter boom. "Construction workers, plumbers, electricians, networking engineers, all of those incredible jobs are being created in the United States. I think it already has created a million jobs, and then the layer above that, look at all the startups that are being created," he claimed. "That's productivity, increasing the GDP, increasing our growth, which also results in increasing how busy we are. But that's the end. AI makes jobs, and hopefully doesn't take jobs." Asked about people already losing work to AI - global financial services group Barclays Bank said only this morning it is chopping 5,000 workers and relying more on AI - Huang argued that technological change has always displaced some jobs while creating others. "Now, with AI, of course, some jobs are not necessary as much as before, or maybe not as interesting as before. And some new jobs and new companies and new businesses are necessary. It's the nature of the world," he stated. On safety, Huang pointed to Nvidia's OpenShell sandbox technology, designed to restrict agents to the resources needed for a task. "If you're making an omelette, you don't need a hammer," he said. But he got hot under the collar when asked about slowing down the pace of AI development while the risks were evaluated, in light of incidents such as AI agents from Anthropic and OpenAI breaking into other computer systems. "You would favor pacing the frontier? I favor them doing whatever they need to do to not bring harm to society," Huang said. "You, sir, if you believe that you should not leave your house because you're inappropriately dressed, or somehow you're going to bring harm to society, could you please not come out?" he told the questioner. "The message from the labs is that there's a collective action problem, and that some minimum standards in coordination would be good here. That's a different question. If you know something is already delivering harm, you got to stop running," he added. Nvidia has a commercial interest in keeping the AI build-out moving. It reported $215.9 billion in revenue for fiscal 2026 and $120 billion in net profit. In the first half of its fiscal 2027, those net profits were already close to the prior year's . The opportunity isn't limited to just chips either. Huang put the price of licensing Nvidia's software stack at about $2,000 per GPU annually. The CEO's domestic vision was also on show. Asked when households could run large AI models, he held up a DGX Spark system. "This computer has a chip called N1X inside, and N1X has 128 gigabytes of memory… It's $4,000. You're right. It's quite expensive. However, that computer was designed to sit on the network in your house, and it would have agents that are used by all of your family members. So it's kind of like a TV. It's sitting in your house. It's shared by everyone, and everybody's agents will be running on DGX Spark," he explained. As an example, Huang said his home agent had researched Berlin's best schnitzel and produced a brochure with restaurant pictures and menus. "So that agent, you know, that computer will become essentially your family's robot. It has no arms and legs, but it's an agent, so it's kind of like a robot. And this one is just for your home. So that's kind of how I see the future. This is pretty affordable. This is a personal computer." Affordable if your net worth is around $180-$190 billion. Maybe not to the average household struggling to pay bills in a cost of living crisis. ®

item.title: Africa faces ‘complex’ Ebola outbreak after virus spread to Nigeria – WHO
item.description: The World Health Organization’s Africa chief warned on Thursday that the continent now faced a “complex” Ebola outbreak after the virus crossed from east Africa to Nigeria, which has reported the first case in the west of the continent. “We are facing a more complex outbreak landscape. Nigeria has confirmed an imported case of Ebola virus disease,” Mohamed Janabi, the regional director for WHO in Africa, told an online media briefing. Nigeria on Tuesday announced an imported case of the Bundibugyo strain behind a major DR Congo outbreak, in a woman, a diplomat who had a history of travel to Uganda. The continent’s most populous nation is the fourth African country affected by the outbreak, which this week came to span the continent, with Kenya in the east reporting nine cases since October 6. The case reignited memories of a widespread outbreak in 2014 that struck several countries in the region and killed more than 11,000 people across west Africa between late 2013 and 2016. Nigeria’s experience in successfully containing the Ebola outbreak in 2014 raised confidence that the country can respond effectively to new public health threats. The DRC’s Ebola epidemic has become the deadliest in the country’s history, killing 4,381 people out of more than 9,000 confirmed cases since mid-May, according to the health authorities. The post Africa faces ‘complex’ Ebola outbreak after virus spread to Nigeria – WHO appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Cardi B Makes Her Tiny Desk Debut With “Bodak Yellow,” “Be Careful” & More | Watch
item.description: Autographed polaroid photo of Cardi B at the NPR Music office for her Tiny Desk Concert set. Photo Credit: NPR Music/Instagram If you thought you knew what a Cardi B live set looked like, think again. The rap superstar recently stepped into the NPR Music office for her debut Tiny Desk Concert, and the atmosphere was nothing short of electric. Word got out fast, drawing one of the biggest crowds the office has ever seen as people from all walks of life lined up to watch hip-hop’s most unfiltered star take over the iconic workspace. Dressed sharply in leather trousers and a power blazer, Cardi brought a refreshingly humble and humorous spirit to the desk, delivering a masterclass in stage presence. Kicking things off with the haunting synths and outright confidence of “ Hello ,” she immediately set the tone before riding that unstoppable energy into a reimagined version of “ ErrTime .” Never one to shy away from versatility, she then shifted gears into deeply personal material, performing the vulnerable “ Man of Your Word ” and “ Be Careful ” while keeping her trademark wit and humor intact. “Change the vibes, change the vibes,” she joked with a smile, before bringing the ultimate party back with “ Up ,” which slid straight into “ AH HA .” To close out the unforgettable set, she treated the packed room to two pivotal anthems from her legendary catalogue: “ Bodak Yellow ,” the breakout hit that started it all, and the boogaloo-heavy crowd-pleaser “ I Like It .” By the end of the set, Cardi was swinging her hips right along with the ecstatic crowd, leaving the room beaming with gratitude and handing out warm hugs to a few lucky audience members. It is safe to say the Desk has never seen anything quite like it. Watch below The post Cardi B Makes Her Tiny Desk Debut With “Bodak Yellow,” “Be Careful” & More | Watch appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today! .
